💡 Key Takeaways
  • von Next Generation am 24.10.2026 in den Kategorien Champions League,Uncategorized mit 0 Kommentaren.
  • Sources indicate that como beat Manchester United 4-1 — and in this case the scoreline really is a fair expression of the game.
  • It has been revealed that cesc Fàbregas’s side demonstrated two things that rarely go together.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

von Next Generation am 24.10.2026 in den Kategorien Champions League,Uncategorized mit 0 Kommentaren.

Sources indicate that como beat Manchester United 4-1 — and in this case the scoreline really is a fair expression of the game. For long stretches the match was one-sided, not in terms of chance volume but in terms of access: Como dictated in every phase where the ball went, who received it, and under what conditions it had to be played on. United never got on terms in any of those phases.

It has been revealed that cesc Fàbregas’s side demonstrated two things that rarely go together. Out of possession, a pressing structure with clear direction, isolation of one side, and man-marking that applied near the ball only for the action in progress while everything around it was already speculating on the second ball. And in possession, a positional game of remarkable technical maturity that ties opponents in, switches play, and works systematically into the space behind them. The 4-1 is therefore less an outlier than evidence of work that has been built up over recent seasons.

This analysis goes through the phases one by one: first Como in possession and United’s response, then the work against the ball from the high press to defending the box, and finally the goals.

Industry observers note that in build-up, Como moved away from their nominal 4-2-3-1 and sat closer to a 4-3-3, with the eights as the real variable: very free in their movement and above all active in the half-spaces. The base structure stayed stable — a flat four plus a six in front of them, sometimes ahead of the line, sometimes slightly behind the forward line.

Recent findings suggest that close to their own goal, Como consistently involved goalkeeper Butez as an additional central player in the build-up. That created a five-against-four against United’s front line — awkward on paper, more awkward still in execution, because Como didn’t use the overload to play through but to tie opponents in. From there, the same shape kept appearing on both the right and the left: centre-back, full-back, a player from the half-position in the eight space, and a six alongside. A diamond that wasn’t an end in itself but had a purpose: the diagonal route out.

Como’s build-up structure. From a 4-1 (flat four), the half-positions with Paz and Perrone are added. Small triangles and diamonds emerge. The three attackers ahead of them create additional options in behind.

Industry observers note that one detail deserves particular attention. At times the full-backs stood not wide but flat, in a half-position. That sounds like a nuance, but it had a clear function: it vacated the wing and created the space the eights could drop into — Paz and Perrone did so regularly. If you don’t occupy the wing yourself, you force the opponent to guard it anyway.

ManU got no access near the ball and left large diagonal spaces open on the far side.

In a recent development, for United’s midfielders this was close to unsolvable. Tielemans, Mount and Andrey Santos spent the whole game struggling to establish any responsibility at all, let alone get into duels. When an eight dropped out, they couldn’t follow, and if one of them was tied in by it, a two-against-one opened up on the far wing. Como didn’t create that situation once; they created it serially.

According to recent reports, the decisive mechanism lay in receiving and relaying the ball. The player in the deeper position usually worked with two touches: the first took the ball backwards, the second relayed it to the free teammate. At the end of every one of those actions stood a player with the game in front of him — and from that open position he could switch play.

Recent findings suggest that what made it possible were the preparatory movements. Paz and captain Da Cunha first lured their markers in the wrong direction and then worked with the head start they’d bought. That head start isn’t only space, it’s above all time: time to control the ball first and relay it second, rather than having to do both in one touch.

It has been revealed that A scene in the 17th minute is typical. Mason Mount steps out, Mazraoui goes into the duel at the same time — nominally United are in an overload here. Only neither of them really gets to the opponent, because both are too late. Paz can therefore calmly take his touch backwards and switch play directly with the second, dissolving the pressure before it had even formed.

Recent findings suggest that when the build-up ran down the right, it demonstrated in a recurring pattern: Paz and Da Cunha took the first touch backwards or inside and then switched with the left foot out of a closed body position. The players they found were systematically in open positions — Milla, the far-side six, or the wing-to-wing connection directly.

In the second half, Como adjusted the shape and more often played with two sixes, to form the diamonds faster and switch to the far-side six faster. Couto stood out in this: the right-back repeatedly played the chip into the six or ten space — six or seven times in a row during one spell. It was mainly Paz who received the ball there and could launch the attack.

In the second half Como focus on those diagonal spaces and look for them mainly with chipped balls.

Especially striking inside the diamond are the rotations between the players. Because of the connections between them, they moved in rotation depending on running path, space and ball movement. The same recurring spaces were re-occupied. Under pressure on the ball carrier, the outer players pushed flat or ran in behind the opponents; the highest player in the diamond burst out of the cover shadow and became the reference point in depth. On a deep pass, the two wide players released and joined the depth, able to offer themselves again immediately in an open body position. If the pass went via the flat wide players, the spaces in front of the newly introduced ball carrier could be run into. Every rotation, every positional adjustment was coordinated with the others and, in the end, produced a stream of pressure-resolving passes while Manchester United chased the press in vain.

Como bridged the middle third exceptionally rapidly, via dribbles at speed and diagonal passes. Behind it stood a recognisable principle: first tie the opponent to one wing, then get behind them via the diagonal, and in the final third do the same thing again. In sum, that produced the shape of a Z — build-up on the right, transition on the left, finish from the right again.

In this example Como pin ManU in the press with their short passing. Thanks to the extra attacker on the ball-near side they can play through the pressure and switch.

It has been revealed that the connections between wingers and striker carried these attacks and were deliberately kept flexible. The wide players sometimes stayed wide, sometimes came short, sometimes tucked inside. Douvikas accordingly either waited deep in front of the line for the chipped ball or, when space opened up on the wing, received the deeper pass and then ran in behind along the wing as soon as the ball sat on the full-back’s open foot. That flexibility produced the overloads on one side, and the overloads produced the central overload.

It has been revealed that in the final third one element was added that is rare in fast transition teams: patience. Como drew opponents towards them with dribbles and short passes, used back-passes when needed, and then switched in front of the block. Da Cunha, Baturina and Paz were the three who could tie opponents in and then find the diagonal. They created the positions on the diagonal, were available to receive, and used their space to apply pressure. The block was usually tied in with short touches, the switch and the position behind the opponent prepared, and quick finishes sought.

In a recent development, the intensity in possession shouldn’t be underestimated. Practically every attack involved at least three or four players, the width was occupied, the centre likewise, and there were multiple options throughout. What they looked for almost every time was the space behind the opponent on the far side — exactly the zone that is closed last when a block shifts across.

Paz brought the right profile for this pattern. A strong left foot cutting inside from the right, he repeatedly dropped into the right-hand blind side of his opponents, got shots away there with few touches, and racked up the most shots of the match. That the finishes generally came off few touches isn’t a detail but the consequence of the time won further back.

As the move continues, Como again look for the blind side of the defenders. Here Douvikas and Paz are positioned in behind, with Da Cunha joining in front of the back line. After briefly pinning the opponents, the switch reaches Da Cunha, who misses the target from distance.

According to recent reports, what carries all of this is the technical execution. Soft passes, sharp ones when the moment called for it, consistently well timed and played into the right foot — for ninety minutes. Passing that secure at that tempo is what makes a variable concept actually retrievable.

United’s basic problem out of possession was the hybrid. They pressed half man-oriented, but with a plus-one in the last line — a construction that forces compromises in both directions. It demands access up front that it doesn’t fund at the back.

Recent findings suggest that there were certainly moments when it worked. When Dalot pushed through into the press on the right and passed his man backwards, a clean man-orientation emerged all the way up to the front — and with it a clear assignment for Mount, out of which the ball could be won. But that stayed the exception. Most of the time Dalot sat too flat out of possession, so United couldn’t trigger the duels up front and went into the press a man short.

It has been revealed that mount was the most conspicuous case in this respect. He barely got into a duel across the whole match because the decision to step out always came too late. Against a team that works with preparatory movements, a late decision is practically the same as none: the opponent already has the head start before the journey even begins.

It has been revealed that on top of that came a problem on the far side. There, United’s winger frequently failed to protect the depth — usually Mbeumo, who jogged back rather than closing the space. But that was precisely the target zone of Como’s diagonal switches. It allowed them to change sides almost at will and regularly find an open structure on the other side.

The second half brought no improvement. The distances to opponents stayed large, and centrally what was actually intended still didn’t materialise. Michael Carrick’s double change at half-time was meant to bring more physicality to the six with Carlos Baleba, but it didn’t solve the problem — the assignments still didn’t work, the duels in the centre still didn’t happen, and the wide positions dragged the eights out further, which opened upcoming spaces.

In a recent development, in the end the energy simply wasn’t there to press with the necessary intensity. United’s press became increasingly static, and a static press against an opponent with this passing quality yields not a single ball win — it only hands them the starting positions they’re looking for anyway.

Como started the game in a high press and sustained it above all in the first half, with isolated spells after the break too. It was triggered on back-passes and goal kicks — and, remarkably, by their own goals: after every strike the team immediately pushed high again instead of managing the lead in a deeper block.

The steering ran consistently towards United’s left build-up side. The reason is personnel: Harry Maguire played there with his weaker left foot as the outside foot, and next to him stood another right-footer in Noussair Mazraoui on the left. Two right-footers on one build-up side means the ball always has to be taken back inside to play on — exactly where Como were closing the door. The press was usually triggered by the left-sided forward, with the ball ending up at either Maguire or Mazraoui.

Pressing structure after the change in the second half.

Industry observers note that in the centre Como defended man-oriented, with both sixes pushing very high and taking flat passes into United’s midfielders out of the game. That removed the short route through the middle as an option and left the long ball. But the long ball triggered nothing for United: the second balls went to Como practically every time.

Sources indicate that that isn’t chance, it’s running work. The sixes consistently tracked the negative pressing paths back, anticipated the long ball early, and were in front of the line before it arrived. Luis Milla covered the most ground of any player on the pitch in this pattern — recovery runs after being played past, doubling up on the ball, attacking the second ball. When the long ball came from Maguire or one of the full-backs, a six was regularly in front of the line with an intense sprint, sealing the centre, taking away the diagonal follow-up passes and attacking the loose balls.

Defending the long ball and extra support on the second ball.

Once the ball was on one side, that side was isolated. The near-side forward had access to the centre-back and dropped back a touch when the pass went to the full-back, so that he covered centre-back and six simultaneously and closed the square pass. The far-side forward marked the goalkeeper. That served two functions at once: it took away United’s escape route via the keeper along with the switch, and it kept a player in position for the moment of the turnover.

The double pivot worked in a deliberate half-position. The near-side six stayed tight to his man, the far-side one dropped slightly behind him — securing the space and at the same time establishing access to the far-side centre-back in United’s back three.

It has been revealed that the last line defended largely man-for-man in the high press, and very tightly. But the decisive detail is the one that carries the whole concept: the man-marking near the ball applied only to the action in progress. Around it, players were already releasing from their assignments and orienting towards the second ball. That is only retrievable at very high intensity — and it’s the reason United’s forced long balls produced not a single usable moment.

In a recent development, when Como dropped a line, the man-orientation at the second height stayed exceptionally high. Here too the back-pass served as the trigger to push up as a unit and tip back into man-marking. If United were in a closed body position, the Comaschi had already pushed up far enough to attack the back-pass at the moment it was played — a pattern that led directly to the 3-0. The half-position was at work there again: closing down level with the centre-back while simultaneously prepared to push through onto the next player deeper.

It has been revealed that in the first half Como still had problems assigning the half-positions against ManU’s 3-2-5. In this example Fernandes moves to the wing, Como fail to establish responsibility and access and are played through at mid-height.

Up to half-time, though, Como had a structural problem with this. The pure man-marking didn’t come off cleanly, because of the two sixes in front of the line, one should really have tucked in and taken over the half-position for the centre-backs. That didn’t happen consistently. The consequence: a centre-back stepped out, the space behind him stayed unoccupied, and that was exactly what United kept attacking.

The pattern of pressing onto Manchester United’s left side continued in the second half, now with Dalot at full-back. The press was still triggered by Douvikas, with the ball-near winger pushing up as a second striker to press the centre-back. Paz focused on the visitors’ ball-near six and Couto pushed through onto Dalot. Through the central connections the game was isolated on one side.

At half-time Como adjusted. One six moved directly into the line, with the far-side winger pushing in onto the six — they now pressed out of a 5-2-1-2. Lucas Da Cunha pressed through from the right onto Maguire, while Nico Paz picked up United’s six. The central forward pressed the central centre-back and from there carried on to the goalkeeper. The far-side wide midfielder and the remaining six were poised — one onto United’s free six, one onto the far-side centre-back — again in that half-position between opponent and the space to be protected.

ManU building up high against the man-oriented Italians.

The effect was immediately visible. Como controlled the half-positions, got access right into the last line throughout, and set the rhythm of the match from then on. The adjustment solved exactly the problem the first half had left open, without changing the underlying principle.

In the final phase Como defended from a very deep line inside the box. That left barely any space behind the line to play into — which United hardly looked for anyway. The visitors attacked little depth and rarely occupied the width in the final third, so Como could stay compact without being punished for it.

In a recent development, accordingly, a lot of players stood very centrally in and in front of the box. That produced numerous cover shadows and a numerical superiority around the ball, which allowed them to steer actively within the block rather than merely react. At times they deliberately steered inside, to guide the opponent into the prepared congestion and cover from a deeper position.

Deep back line in the box, centre closed and play steered inside. The box defending allowed the English side shots from distance.

The crucial point is that Como left the gaps open not despite this set-up but because of it. If you pack the box and secure the depth, you give up the space in front of the line — and that is exactly where United were supposed to shoot from.

It has been revealed that the numbers vindicate the decision. Taking the conceded goal out of the box, Como allowed nine shots from outside the penalty area across ninety minutes, worth roughly 0.24 xG combined; only three of them were even on target. On top of that, of the four shots inside the box, two came from at least 14 to 15 metres and effectively belong in the long-range category as well. United accepted the invitation, and the shooting quality was perfectly decent — it’s just that with that scoring probability over a whole match, the most likely outcome is precisely what happened.

Tracking the ball for the first goal.

Recent findings suggest that 1-0, Nico Paz (2′) — The goal comes before United are even set. Como take the goal kick swiftly and play straight to the full-back, luring the visitors into the press — only not cleanly. Mason Mount triggers the pressure and is played past, and on the second ball he goes into the duel as well instead of holding the middle and looking for the space where he could pick the ball up. That is exactly what opens the centre, the space for the second ball is there, and Paz can play it through.

What follows is the transition principle in its purest form: a quick switch to the diagonal side, then short passes against a very deep line. Matheus Cunha doesn’t pick up the player behind him and leaves the ten space open, where Paz is standing. He needs two touches because neither Cunha from above nor Maguire from his distance gets into the duel. Lammens, for his part, doesn’t defend the goal with his cover shadow but takes the near post — which leaves the far corner to a strong left foot. The curled finish into it is quality, though.

2-0, Anastasios Douvikas (49′, assist Paz) — Same zone, same cause. Bryan Mbeumo doesn’t choose to shut the centre but closes the centre-back, which creates the space for Da Cunha, who drives forward and plays Martin Baturina in. Centrally, Mount again fails to pick up his man. Out wide, Amad Diallo, introduced at half-time, generates no pressure centrally, so Mazraoui can’t take over the deep wide player in the first place.

It has been revealed that the result is Paz behind the opponent, in the ten space, dribbling unopposed at goal. Matthijs de Ligt establishes no reference to Douvikas’s run in behind and slips as well — a one-against-one with the goalkeeper that Douvikas finishes coolly.

It has been revealed that 3-0, Nico Paz (57′) — The only goal that comes directly out of the work against the ball. Como are in the midfield press in a closed position with access to the inside lane, win the ball there and punish a lapse of concentration in the visitors’ build-up. At the end, Paz is alone in front of Lammens again.

4-0, Jacobo Ramón (76′, assist Kaiki) — This goal comes from a longer possession spell and shows the assignment problem in its clearest form. Mazraoui is too narrow and has no access to the wide player. Diallo stands in the space with access to neither the central player nor the full-back nor the winger — an orientation that doesn’t work in any direction.

According to recent reports, como switch to Máximo Perrone, who can slide the ball out wide because the space is simply free. From there comes the cross from an open body position, and in the centre Como run a two-against-one at the end of which Ramón scores.

According to recent reports, 4-1, Joshua Zirkzee (90′) — Como’s only lapse, and one in a phase in which the team had already dropped very deep. United get the ball to the wing, it’s two against two in the box, and the cross is initially only feinted. Zirkzee orients himself well forwards at that moment, while Como’s defenders are already stepping out after the feinted cross. Diallo’s ball in behind the line is strong, the offside call is razor-thin in his favour, and Zirkzee takes two touches before finishing one-against-one with the goalkeeper. A blemish, not a structural problem.

The common denominator — Three of Como’s four goals come in the same zone: the space in front of and behind United’s line that nobody takes responsibility for. Mount is involved in two of those scenes through an assignment he never establishes, Diallo in two more after coming on. Nico Paz is at the heart of three of the four goals, twice as scorer, once as the provider — always out of the opponent’s blind side.

Como’s 4-1 has one common cause across every phase, and it lies less in any single idea than in its execution under continuous load. Out of possession they steered, isolated and speculated on the second ball — with man-marking that applied near the ball only for the action in progress and was already dissolved around it. In possession they tied opponents in, switched play and worked systematically into the space behind. Both require eleven players to anticipate a teammate’s decision, and both functioned over the full distance.

In a recent development, the connecting detail is the half-position. In the press, the far-side six stood between opponent and the space to be protected; in possession, the eights worked out of the same zone, and the full-backs occupied it flat in order to vacate the wing for exactly those players. Como, in other words, occupied the position in both directions from which two jobs can be done at once — which is why the side could neither be played past in the press nor be pinned in the build-up.

In a recent development, for United the diagnosis is more uncomfortable than the result. The problem wasn’t individual errors but that the team never, in any phase, got into the duels it needed. The mixture of half man-orientation and a plus-one in the last line funded no access up front, and without access every decision is made too late — from Mount in the centre to Mbeumo failing to secure the far-side depth. Carrick’s double change at half-time was meant to bring physicality to the six with Carlos Baleba, but it changed nothing about the assignments, and in Diallo a player came on wide who reached neither one opponent nor the other in his space. That the energy ran out in the end was a consequence rather than a cause.

Industry observers note that that leaves the context. A 4-1 against Manchester United is no proof in itself, and Como’s finishing was exceptionally efficient on the night. What demonstrated regardless of the result, though, is a team with a recognisable, rehearsed answer in all four phases of the game — and one that put a technical maturity on the pitch in possession that you wouldn’t readily credit to a side promoted two years ago.

According to recent reports, dans la rubrique Fenêtre sur corps de la Pravda Mag, l'humoriste Léandre parle évidemment des Verts. Extraits.

"Enfant, je faisais beaucoup de foot. J'y ai joué jusqu'à mes 15 ans, mais j'étais très mauvais. Aujourd'hui encore, j'adore. J'ai commencé à aimer parce que ça me rapprochait de mon père. Ça nous faisait un sujet de conversation. Parfois, je me demande si j'aime sincèrement le foot ou si c'est juste pour avoir un lien avec mon père. J'ai une vingtaine de maillots de l'ASSE, des vieux et des récents. Certains étaient à mon grand-père et à mon père.

Je supporte l'AS Saint-Étienne. C'est transgénérationnel : mon grand-père était fan, mon père aussi. Petit, mon père m'achetait tous les maillots. C'est très jouissif d'être autant supporter d'un club. Quand je vois ceux de Sainté sauter ensemble, il y a un truc d'amour, d'union, qui peut me faire pleurer premier degré. Je vais à Geoffroy-Guichard au moins 3 ou 4 fois par an. Depuis peu, ils m'invitent et m'envoient des maillots ! Ça me rend fier.".

Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start

💡 Key Takeaways

  • This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.

This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

According to recent reports, he called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was. “We needed patience on one hand, but also to be passionate and tough. We had the chance [to score] and took it,” he noted.

Newcastle have reached the semi-finals of this competition three times in the last four years, but struggled to get any sort of tempo going against their Championship opponents.

You could argue the winning goal came against the run of play late in the second half, moments after Millwall substitute Taïryk Arconte had smashed a low shot against the post.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

Given they were missing 13 players because of injury, this was a brave display from Alex Neil’s side. They frustrated Newcastle for more than an hour, nullifying their attack, to the point where Jaissle’s team looked as though they had run out of ideas.

That was until Lewis Hall combined with Matias Fernandez-Pardo down the left and his drilled cross found Willock who cleverly used the angle to pass the ball into the net. Willock has been rejuvenated under Jaissle. He looked certain to be sold this summer but is now starting regularly under a newly introduced manager in the number 10 role his system demands. It has been a nice redemption arc for the former Arsenal academy graduate.

Moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

Sources indicate that the victory is all that matters and extends Jaissle’s unbeaten start to five games. Given he arrived just three weeks before the start of the season, that deserves praise even if it is obvious there is a lot of work to be done to improve their offensive play.

Playing in their lilac, or should that be Parma-violet, third kit for the first time, Newcastle looked off colour in the first half. Even though Jaissle named a strong team packed with experience of English cup ties, they struggled to overpower Millwall.

There were a few half-chances as Willock forced a save and Jacob Murphy fired over. There was a header missed from a corner by Sven Botman, which should have hit the target and Yoane Wissa also mistimed his jump after finding space for another header.

According to recent reports, millwall’s two centre-backs, Jake Cooper and Caleb Taylor were immense, flinging themselves in the way of every shot and clearing every loose ball that came into their vicinity. Given their injuries, this was a performance full of fight and defiance from the home side.

However, there was also an absence of quality in the final third from Newcastle, the same lack of cohesion and incision that was apparent at home to Bournemouth last weekend and in the first half away at Tottenham Hotspur.

It meant Millwall were happy to play for set-pieces close to the Newcastle box and Taylor got in front of his marker, flashing a header wide of the post.

That lacklustre first half meant Jaissle’s side had mustered just five shots on target in five halves of football since the 3-2 win over West Bromwich Albion in the previous round of the Carabao Cup.

According to recent reports, millwall started the second period like a side sensing Newcastle were vulnerable. A thunderbolt from Jenson Metcalfe, after the visitors had struggled to clear two crosses, almost gave them a spectacular lead.

Newcastle saw lots of the ball. Millwall were happy enough to let them have it given how little they were hurting them.

It has been revealed that so much of Newcastle’s play was slow and cumbersome. Their set-piece delivery was also largely inept.

Neil’s side retained a threat and came so close to taking the lead when, not for the first time, a long ball forward caught the Newcastle defence out of shape and Tino Livramento’s mistake allowed Arconte to run clear and hit the post from a tight angle.

It has been revealed that well in, @Joewillock! 💪 pic.twitter.com/5a8G7lzD3H.

Speaking after the game, Millwall manager Alex Neil mentioned: “I’m very proud, I don’t think we deserved to lose that game.

Sources indicate that “We had some good moments, and we got done by a bit of sucker punch at the end. But I’m very proud of the lads.”.

According to recent reports, as for their injury problems, he added: “I didn’t bring the teenagers on as a token gesture, I need to keep the first-team players fit. We’re really at bare bones.

But we beat Bolton at the weekend, got a couple of defeats before that but we started the season really well and once we get everybody back, we’ll be in good shape.”.

With the first of the 16 teams through tonight, the draw won’t take place until most of the teams have played next week.

The draw will be shown on Sky Sports on Wednesday 16th Sept, after Manchester United play Brighton. Man City vs Norwich will be the only game outstanding then.

The third round had to be spread over two weeks as the nine Premier League sides in UEFA competitions entered the tournament in this round, as the same time as their Champions League and Europa League fixtures began. To avoid clubs facing clashes, the EFL split the fixtures across the two gameweeks.

Still got some more post-match to come for you, but we’ve got scores from all our matches tonight now:.

Crystal Palace 3-0 Middlesbrough.

Leyton Orient 1-3 Bradford City.

From the Champions League, Man City held out against Porto to win 2-0.

“I think we had a lot of chances in the first half, and we went in a half-time saying we need to  take our chances, so I’m glad we came out in the second half and we did,” mentioned Willock after the match.

According to recent reports, “100% [the competition is crucial], we’ve won it before so it’s very important to us, but every game is important to us. Especially with a upcoming coach and a lot of new players, we wanted to start the new season well. I think we started really well and we need to continue and this was a big game in keeping that momentum.”.

"We mentioned at half-time we NEED to take our chances"Lewis Hall and Joe Willock react to Newcastle's win over Millwall 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/NDF3laD8nT.

Take a look at the match-winner from Joe Willock:.

Moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

The goal came minutes after Millwall were inches away from taking the lead themselves, as Arconte was denied by the post:.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

We’ll be bringing you more from the post-match now.

Joe Willock has done enough for Newcastle to reach the fourth round and keep the travelling fans singing all the way back to the North-East.

It won’t go down in history as the greatest Carabao fixture, but Newcastle found a way to keep their momentum going and give Matthias Jaissle a win on his cup debut.

Newcastle aren’t taking any risks as Hornicek sends the ball long, and the players keep looking to send the ball down-field.

Recent findings suggest that seconds to go now. Marschall sends it long for one last effort, but it is cleared out of the box...

It has been revealed that willock has come off now for Newcastle’s own teenager, Sean Steur. A few more minutes and the man now on the bench with have done enough to send his side through to the next round.

We’re into the final minutes as Millwall are throwing everything at this.

Millwall are not out of this yet, as Neghli comes down the left side, twisting his way into the box past his defender – but having done the hard work, his shot flashes low across goal.

Some more changes, as Ramsey comes off for Newcastle, replaced by Lewis Miley.

A double change for the hosts as Dykes and Kelly come off for Regan Monty and Alfie Massey – the former just 15 years old.

Seconds later, another teenager takes to the pitch for Millwall as Osei-Tutu is replaced by 17-year-old Tristan Parkes.

Industry observers note that newcastle almost have another! From the sublime to the ridiculous, as Willock makes another run, this time down the left, and passes the ball onto the edge of the box where Elanga meets it in space. He lets it run, before taking his shot, but it is straight to Marschall.

Recent findings suggest that finally Newcastle have their breakthrough! They punish Millwall as Fernandez-Pardo feeds Hall on the left, who cuts inside and slips the ball across goal, finding Willock to redirect the ball to slot it home.

You can hear the travelling fans now!

It has been revealed that marschall releases Arconte with a long ball and he turns Livramento to find huge amounts of space on the right side. He races into the box and takes a shot from close range, aiming for his near post, but is denied by the woodwork and the rebound hits the seated Hornicek. The keeper is lucky to not concede an own goal, as the ball bounces up and over his leg.

Issoufou again racing down the right side, before cutting inside and taking a shot with his left foot. Hall, who has been so crucial in the Newcastle attack, throws himself at the shot, and it flies high for Hornicek to collect.

Replays show that González, who Millwall players claimed had handled the ball earlier, leant down to clear with his shoulder.

Issoufou sends a great ball in for Millwall from the right side, but it is cleared by a Newcastle player, accompanied by cries for handball.

The game is opening up now as Newcastle make a run of their own, with Willock creating an opening for Elanga to take the ball to the edge of the box, before Taylor slides in to block his shot.

Millwall could absolutely win this with a smash-and-grab with less than 20 minutes to go. They are pushing for it but are lacking some attacking quality to finish the job.

From six shots they’ve had two on target, compared to Newcastle’s three on target from 20.

Fernandez-Pardo gets his first look at the ball, making a very quick run down across the centre of the field to the left side, but Osei-Tutu stays with him and takes him all the way to the back line before giving up a corner.

Elanga takes the corner, punched away by the keeper but no one goes to finish the job and Newcastle get another corner.

Metcalfe, who had his red card overturned this week, is the first player to go in the book for a mistimed challenge on Ramsey.

Just a reminder that there is no extra time, so if we’re all square after 90 minutes, it’s straight to a penalty shoot-out.

Willock gets the ball on the edge of the area and passes it on a quick turn to Barnes just inside the box, but there was not much on his shot and Marschall collects easily.

According to recent reports, double change now for Newcastle as Wissa and Murphy come off, replaced by Elanga and Fernandez-Pardo as Jaissle looks for pace. Schar is handed the armband.

Free kick for Newcastle, right on the corner of the box. Murphy takes, but it hits the wall 10 feet away, and bounces straight back to him. His cross into the box is headed out, and for all the opportunities Newcastle have created, they are yet to find the breakthrough.

We’ve also had a double change for Millwall as Esse and Lovelace have come off, replaced by Issoufou and Arconte.

What colour would you describe this Newcastle away shirt? They look like the sweets Purple Violet to me. Although would you call it an all Lilac number?

It’s the first time they have worn their third kit. Not sure whether I like it or not. Shame The Den isn’t a sell out although I’m told tickets were priced at £31 and Millwall have a lot of injuries too.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle get another corner after a run from Willock. The delivery from Hall creates a good amount of confusion in the box and Marschall isn’t sure whether to stay on his line or come out to punch it away. From within the bodies, Wissa tries to get a shot off from close range but it bounces and the keeper easily collects.

González commits another foul, pulling down Esse, to give Millwall another free kick from 40 yards out.

The ball meets Taylor at the back post, but he meets it in the air and can’t quite direct it either into goal or back into the six-yard box, so it goes out for a Newcastle goal kick.

Another half chance for Millwall as Dykes feeds Kelly on the right side, who runs into the box and gets caught between passing the ball in and taking the shot, with the ball going high over the box.

Another great challenge from Osei-Tutu as Willock makes a run into the box, but is brought down by a well-timed tackle from the right-back.

The corner from Hall is better, but headed out and cleared.

Barnes again with space on the left side and he sends a ball fizzing low across the box to the far post but Neghli is able to lean on Murphy to stop him making contact.

It has been revealed that scramble for Newcastle as the ball is sent by Dykes to Neghli free at the far post, who puts the ball into a very dangerous area just in front of goal and everyone jumps on. Newcastle get to it first, managing to clear it from the goal mouth. It is cleared outside the box and it bounces to unmarked Metcalfe, who takes a thunderous shot, putting his laces through the ball but he is unable to keep it down and it goes over the bar.

Promising restart for the home side.

Despite Alex Neil’s premonitions, no changes for Millwall at the break.

Right-back change for Newcastle, as Dedic comes off and Tino Livramento comes on.

The earlier kick-offs of the Carabao third round have just started their second periods, but here are the latest scores:.

Crystal Palace 1-0 Middlesbrough.

Leyton Orient 1-1 Bradford City.

Aston Villa won their opening Champions League fixture 3-2 against Club Brugge, while Man City are still goalless against Porto, which you can follow with our live blog here.

And that’s the last action of the half, as just one minute was added on and that was taken up by Newcastle’s corner.

Nothing separates the two sides at the half, thought the visitors have dominated in terms of possession and chances.

Millwall have held fast and will be happy to be finishing the half level. We may see some changes from them after the break.

The game is opening up before half-time, and Newcastle go again with Hall and Barnes. Osei-Tutu does well to wait before going in to block Barnes’s shot and send the ball behind for another Newcastle corner.

Recent findings suggest that the delivery is once again poor, but Schar is pulled down inside the box by Taylor and is furious that nothing was given. There’s no VAR so there’s no review to consider – but looking at replays, Millwall were very lucky to get away with that foul.

Cooper makes a perfect pass down the left sideline, allowing Neghli to find space and forcing Newcastle to clear it away fo a Millwall corner.

The ball in is promising but Hornicek gets to it and punches it away, but the hosts keep the pressure on.

Baggott floats another ball across the box towards the right back post, but Hornicek easily collects the ball as Neghli can’t quite connect.

According to recent reports, newcastle moving the ball well again across midfield and it comes to Schar, who runs into space and gets a low shot away, around 40 yards out. It  takes a slight deflection on its way, going just wide of the post.

González is not having his best night and makes a silly foul against Dykes on the sideline, giving the hosts another set piece. The swinging ball in is not nearly as good as last time, and only reaches the first man, Newcastle’s Ramsey.

Sources indicate that millwall get a free kick, and the delivery is good, allowing Taylor to connect on the header inside the box. He beats Hornicek but the header rolls just wide of the post, to the groans of the home fans.

Hall goes short with the corner and Dedic has lots of time to cross the ball in from the right. It’s headed away but Millwall can’t break on the counter.

That sums up the game pretty well: not much finishing quality from Newcastle but Millwall not creating much from their limited spells of possession.

Newcastle pushing again. Another ball pulled back by Barnes finds Ramsey at the top of the box, and his ball in connects with Wissa. Newcastle’s captain can’t head it in the right direction though and Millwall survive again.

The spell of pressure results in another corner for the visitors – and now we’re getting some pushing in the six-yard box.

It has been revealed that I think Millwall have done well. They have limited Newcastle to half chances and the odd set piece threat. They have made things really difficult for the visitors, crowding them out of space on the edge of the area.

When the home side have advanced up the pitch the Newcastle defence has not looked particularly secure.

As we reach the half-hour mark, Newcastle have 10 shots to Millwall’s one, though they sit one apiece on shots on target.

Esse gets caught on his heels as Hall pulls a long ball back on the left, and in the crowd at the top of the box Willock takes a shot, pulling it wide – cheers from the home crowd again.

Industry observers note that first piece of good attacking play from Millwall as Neghli and Baggott work on the overlap. Baggott lofts a high ball to the back post, where Dykes gets a foot on it on the volley, but he can’t quite get over it and it’s easily picked up by Hornicek.

Industry observers note that barnes and Ramsey combine again down the left, with the midfielder trying to feed Barnes on his run. The pass has too much on it though, and as it runs out the back it’s met with jeers from the home fans for a goal kick.

According to recent reports, wissa breaks away down the centre of the field, with Barnes on his left, using him as a decoy. Wissa takes the shot though and it is blocked by a sliding defender.

Newcastle hit 20 minutes in with 68 per cent possession but nothing to show yet for their efforts. You feel like it will only be a matter of time though.

In a recent development, another Newcastle corner, swung in well and Botman comes charging in, beating cooper to a free header. The defender heads it over the bar and holds his head in his hands. The visitors could definitely be a goal up by now.

Hall’s free-kick is met by the first man Metcalfe who heads it away to atone for his foul and Newcastle remain stymied.

Millwall will have expected Newcastle to dominate the ball but they are really pushing for an opener, especially down the left side with Barnes and Hall.

According to recent reports, again, Newcastle coming down the wings, this time on the left. Esse picks the ball up but loses it and Willock picks it up and takes a shot on his right foot with good power but sends it straight at Marschall. The debut keeper parries it away and it’s cleared by a  Millwall header.

Willock comes down the left soon after and is fouled by Metcalfe to get a free kick in a good spot outside the box.

Murphy gets a shot off after Dedic picks up a long ball on the right side and crosses it back towards the middle of the field. Murphy gets on it and takes the shot inside the box off his left foot but it sails over the bar.

González gives the ball away cheaply and Metcalfe picks it up, but unable to move it forward.

Newcastle will need to make sure they don’t get complacent in defence.

Millwall having a spell of possession, the counter-attack looking like their best option but as they move down the right hand side, Lovelace makes a late challenge to get the ball back and fouls Wissa.

Newcastle advancing, with Dedic and Ramsey moving the ball across midfield. Barnes gets the ball on the left of the box, and his ball is in knocked out and Newcastle get the first corner of the game.

Nothing comes of it as it is sent in high and long over the box.

Industry observers note that fair to say both teams are settling, but Millwall try and create a chance with Lovelace, though it’s intercepted. Dykes takes a bit of a knock and is slow to get up.

Here we go in south London, and Millwall get us started.

Just a reminder of the teams starting today:.

Starting XI: Filip Marschall; Jordi Osei-Tutu, Caleb Taylor, Jake Cooper, Elkan Baggott; Lyndon Dykes, Jenson Metcalfe; Camiel Neghli, Daniel Kelly, Romain Esse; Zak Lovelace.

Substitutes: Regan Monty, Tristan Parkes, Sacha Vieira, George Beaumont, Yanis Issoufou, George Evans, Taïryk Arconte, Alfie Massey, Zak Sturge.

Starting XI: Lukás Hornícek; Lewis Hall, Fabian Schär, Amar Dedic, Sven Botman; Jacob Murphy, Nico González; Jacob Ramsey, Harvey Barnes, Joe Willock; Yoane Wissa.

Substitutes: Tino Livramento, Anthony Elanga, Malick Thiaw, Nick Pope, Lewis Miley, Bazoumana Touré, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, Aladji Bamba, Sean Steur.

The teams are coming out of the tunnel, and both home and away fans in the Den are already in loud voice. Kick off on the way!

"We've tried to find the right balance" ⚖️Matthias Jaissle on his team selection for tonight's match with Millwall ⚫️ pic.twitter.com/kiRRxAgLk8.

We’re just a few minutes away from kick off in south London, but Bournemouth have scored the first goal of the third round, with Ryan Christie putting his side ahead against Lincoln.

Alex Neil has not minced his words over his squad’s injury crisis. His team is down 13 players, which the coach says has “definitely forced” his hand in terms of squad rotation.

Playing two matches a week in the “relentless” Championship has turned his squad selection into a “needs must scenario” and he even admitted he “may need to make a couple of changes at half-time depending on how the game goes”.

Matthias Jaissle is clearly taking this competition seriously and having started the league well, he is still trying to get the fans onside and create momentum for his team.

At the same time, Telegraph Sport have reported that Ross Wilson, the sporting director, has warned there will have to be more departures in future windows. Having lost Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães in 12 months, there will be yet be more upheaval.

You can read Luke Edwards’ full story on that here.

The Premier League teams playing in European competitions enter the EFL Cup in this round, with all 16 fixtures being played over five match days. As well as tonight’s games there will be:.

Peterborough United vs Barnsley (7.45pm).

Fleetwood Town vs Sheffield United (7.45pm).

Manchester City vs Norwich City (7.30pm).

*all kick-off at 8pm, unless stated otherwise.

Newcastle have named a strong side – probably the strongest they could field when factoring in senior players needing game time – to take on Millwall in the Carabao Cup.

Industry observers note that jacob Ramsey impressed coming off the bench against Bournemouth last weekend and manager Matthias Jaissle refused to sanction winger Jacob Murphy’s transfer to Nottingham Forest late in the window. Both deserve a chance to impress from the start.

Veteran centre back Fabian Schar comes in for Malick Thiaw, but those are the only three changes from the side that drew with Bournemouth.

Jaissle insisted he would take the competition seriously and the teamsheet proves it, but it also raises questions about some of Newcastle’s summer recruitment.

Bazoumana Toure cost £42m but was withdrawn at half time in the win over West Brom in the previous round, which means Harvey Barnes does not get a rest. That’s a lot of money to spend on a winger who has not looked Premier League ready so far.

In a recent development, aladji Bamba, a £30m signing from Monaco, has not started a game yet and has been an unused substitute since the opening game against Liverpool. He remains on the bench.

Even Sean Steur, who has looked good since his summer move from Ajax, cannot dislodge another more recent arrival in former Manchester City midfielder Nico González.

Having made a total of eight new signings in a much-vaunted summer rebuild, Jaissle only started three of them against Bournemouth and only two start tonight at The Den.

Early days but this was one of the main reasons Eddie Howe quit – he did not think the likes of Toure, Steur and Bamba were ready to play first team football.

The visitors have arrived in south London.

We've made it to South East London 👋 pic.twitter.com/nh8Fpa37xT.

Crystal Palace vs Middlesbrough.

How your Lions line-up tonight 🔢 pic.twitter.com/wEp6qLIz4Y.

Welcome to tonight’s live coverage of Millwall vs Newcastle United, as the Geordies travel to south London for the third round of the Carabao Cup.

Industry observers note that newcastle held off West Brom in their second-round match, with Harvey Barnes scoring two second-half goals to see his side through. It was a mighty comeback, after Isaac Price scored early to stun the crowd at St James’ Park. Bazoumana Toure equalised for Matthias Jaissle’s side just before half-time, and Barnes, his replacement in the second half, put them ahead minutes after the restart. West Brom pulled it back to 2-2 with a penalty converted by Price after Lewis Hall was deemed to have handled the ball in the box, but Barnes got his second just nine minutes from full-time and the hosts were able to see out the match to progress.

Alex Neil’s Millwall have reached round three via a 0-1 win over Cambridge United, following a penalty shoot-out in the first round to beat QPR. They come into this tie with a squad stretched thin, as they have been hit with an injury crisis a month into the upcoming season. Millwall have confirmed that they will be without Casper De Norre, Josh Coburn, Tristan Crama, Alfie Doughty, Mathis Servais, Ryan Leonard, Mihailo Ivanovic, Lukas Jensen and Luke Cundle.

Both sides sit seventh in their respective leagues, with Millwall on a record of three wins and two losses this season, while Newcastle remain unbeaten (two draws and a win).

Newcastle will hoping to progress smoothly in a tournament that they have recently enjoyed good form in – winners in 2025 and semi-finalists last season – and with Millwall dealing with a bare bones squad, the Championship side are the underdogs on paper going into this fixture.

But, as always, anything can happen, so let us know your score prediction in the comments and we’ll be bringing you team news soon!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Après avoir affronté et péniblement éliminé la meilleure attaque de National 1, Sainté va défier samedi (19h) dans le Chaudron la pire défense de Ligue 3.

En effet, si l’ASSE a sur le papier le tirage le moins favorable des clubs de Ligue 2 (les 11 autres rescapés affrontent des clubs de N1, N2 ou Regionale), on notera que Villefranche est bien mal en point dans sa division. Au point que le club situé 30km au nord de Lyon a changé de coach début octobre, en enrôlant Hakim Malek (ex-coach de Martigues alors en L2).

Actuellement 17e sur 18 avec 2 victoires, 2 nuls et déjà 9 défaites, Villefranche s’est incliné (2-4) ce week-end à Bastia, alors que le club semblait aller un peu mieux depuis l’arrivée de Malek qui, avant cette défaite avait pris 4pts en 3 matchs de championnat et battu aisément Paray le monial (formation de R2) en Coupe (3-0).

According to recent reports, néanmoins, avec 30 buts encaissés en 13 matchs (soit 8 de plus que la 2e pire défense de la L3 !), Villefranche bat des records, bien au-delà de la pire défense de L2 (Rodez, 24 buts encaissés) et de L1 (Auxerre et Le Havre, 25 buts encaissés), mais également plus que toute autre équipe de N1 ou N2 (qui ont certes disputé moins de journées). Outre la défaite à Bastia, deux autres fessées subies à l’extérieur en septembre à Fleury (1-6) et au Puy (1-4) confirment en particulier la fragilité des Caladois loin de chez eux.

Cette très poreuse défense ne nous est pas totalement inconnue puisqu’y évoluent deux anciens verts (Marvin Tshibuabua très récemment rejoint par Maedine Makhloufi prêté par Dunkerque) qu'on imagine très motivés à l'idée de faire mentir ces chiffres.

Re-live Daily Mail Sport's live coverage for the latest updates from Anfield as Mauricio Pochettino took charge of Manchester United for the first time at rivals Liverpool in the Premier League.

Right then! That's all from us here. Thanks for your company throughout today.

Sources indicate that congratulations to our Liverpool readers - I'm sure you'll enjoy tonight. As for the United fans... hopefully it gets better for you soon.

According to recent reports, I'll leave you with Ollie Holt's take from the ground, which you can check out by clicking below. A very good read, I must say.

Liverpool's 4-0 win over Man Utd demonstrated just how much Poch has to do.

OLIVER HOLT AT ANFIELD: Omar Berrada, the United chief executive, looked colder and colder in the chill and, beside him, Jason Wilcox, the director of football, slid deeper and deeper into his coat.

Now the international break is done and domestic football is back up and running, the football truly does not stop as we approach the Christmas period.

It's Europe in midweek, and these two sides are, of course, in the Champions League.

Liverpool will travel to Belgium to take on Club Brugge on Wednesday, while United jet to Portugal to take on Sporting on the same day.

Mauricio Pochettino will then take charge of his first home game when United host Brentford in the Premier League on Saturday, with Liverpool making the short trip to Everton for the derby on Sunday.

Bruno Fernandes, Manchester United captain, on BBC Sport:.

Gary Neville, former Man United defender, on Sky Sports:.

If you couldn't tell already, these are dark days for Manchester United.

Sources indicate that I know, I know, we haven't stopped going on about it. I mean, it's hard after watching them get pumped by their biggest rivals away from home. Oh yeah, and they're in the relegation zone in November...

United will end the day in 19th position in the Premier League, with this the first time since November 1986 that they have been within the bottom two places of the league table having played at least 10 matches (21st in that case).

Pochettino needs to change things rapidly, very quickly.

That is the chant that will be going through Andoni Iraola's head tonight; he just loves playing Manchester United.

In a recent development, iraola just never loses to United; he is now unbeaten in all of his seven Premier League matches against Manchester United. That was his third win in that run, too.

The only manager to record a longer unbeaten run against the Red Devils in the competition is one of his predecessors, Jurgen Klopp (eight between 2018 and 2022).

Liverpool certainly picked the right man for this rivalry.

Liverpool's 4-0 win over Man Utd showed just how much Poch has to do.

OLIVER HOLT AT ANFIELD: Omar Berrada, the United chief executive, looked colder and colder in the chill and, beside him, Jason Wilcox, the director of football, slid deeper and deeper into his coat.

I reckon Liverpool fans will have been all over this already, while Manchester United supporters will be steering well clear of YouTube.

But anyway, the highlights are out, and it's my job to share them with all of you.

Liverpool love battering Manchester United in the modern era, don't they?

I mean, they seem to do it every couple of seasons...

Since the start of the 2021-22 season, Liverpool have four wins by four or more goals against Manchester United. Don't forget they beat them 3-0 under Arne Slot at Old Trafford during their title-winning season, too.

Those four wins are the most any Premier League team has achieved against another across all competitions.

And what makes it sweeter is that it's against their biggest rivals.

Industry News: Man City survive tunnel clash and Porto fury thanks to Haaland double

📅 08 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5255 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.
  • Sources indicate that so much for the new group stage of the competition taking time to warm up.
  • It has been revealed that and City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.

Sources indicate that so much for the new group stage of the competition taking time to warm up. This clash was a hot-blooded, bitter contest that spilt over in the tunnel at half-time, with players getting separated and tempers rising.

It has been revealed that and City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games. With Enzo Maresca, it looks like it will be all-out attack to get the best out of this team.

Industry observers note that they can look nervous at the back, particularly with the ball at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s feet, but have attacking weapons to hurt any team in this elite competition. This was a performance that their rivals will take note of.

“It was a complete performance on and off the ball for 95 minutes,” was Maresca’s assessment.

City will certainly scare the traditional heavyweights with Haaland leading their attack and taking an axe to Porto’s defence like he does with logs in his back garden. It was his 58th and 59th goal in 59 games in the Champions League, with his latest an expertly directed header off a post and a calm side-footed finish.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s.

There is an argument that Pep Guardiola could have achieved more in the Champions League, given City’s dominance in domestic football. They have been knocked out by Real Madrid in the last three seasons but this is a newly introduced City, different personnel and even a new look.

They wore their black and yellow away kit, inspired by “Manchester’s iconic worker bee” according to Puma, and grafted their way to victory here. Non-stop running going forward, and scrapping with Porto, too.

In a recent development, the Portuguese champions were not happy with Marc Guéhi’s challenge on Gabri Veiga and claimed an elbow was used, with the row carrying on in the tunnel at half-time with security guards separating the players. Rúben Dias also appeared to nudge a Porto official on his way to the dressing room.

“I didn’t see anything but anyway, you can ask how many times you see me or my bench stand up? Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times do you see their bench? So...” Maresca added.

Only Dias and Haaland remain from the starting line-up from the Champions League triumph three years ago, so this is essentially a upcoming team with a new manager.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw.

Phil Foden, on as a sub in that game, started at Estádio do Dragão after his horse Wreck It Ronnie defeated Najidi Storm, which started the Goodwood race with 1-33 odds and is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. The rest of the team are new to City’s challenge.

That includes Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, who was part of a £320m midfield refresh following the departure of Rodri, who was named among the Ballon d’Or nominees a few hours before kick-off to highlight the experience and class City have lost.

Recent findings suggest that bouaddi, who cost £81.4m from Lille, made a good start in his full debut. The Moroccan teenager is neat on the ball and gets around the pitch, with the next step being able to dominate games like his predecessor.

“In his last game he lost two balls and stayed calm and was back in our box,” Maresca stated. “This shows how good he is because any player after two [poor] passes panics, but he is just 18. Erling, Rúben, Mateo [Kovacic], they can manage these kind of games better, but you don’t expect it from a guy of 18. I didn’t see him panic.”.

By Bouaddi’s side in midfield was Enzo Fernández, who sought to drive forward into space when City counter-attacked. He was among the players who, along with Dias, were reminded of their Benfica history by the home fans.

Industry observers note that diogo Costa tends to be linked with a move to the Premier League every summer, but has been a one-club man for his career so far. But he indicated why clubs are looking at him with his first-half saves to deny Haaland and Rayan Cherki.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was in the press box at half-time and would have been impressed with the saves, although he was not in his seat when Haaland scored the first goal, which came 94 seconds after the restart.

According to recent reports, city had worked the ball around the penalty area, with Antoine Semenyo drawing out Costa before laying off to Fernández. Haaland’s header from the cross had such precision that the goalkeeper did not dive as it angled in off a post.

Still, Porto had their chances with Alberto Costa heading wide from a corner and William Gomes charging down a Donnarumma kick – with City’s most nervous moments coming when they passed around their back line.

It has been revealed that man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn.

But Haaland sealed the win as the game ticked into stoppage time, finding the bottom corner from Rayan Aït-Nouri’s cutback.

It has been revealed that “It was an amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it would be a difficult fight, man against man, they are a top team,” Haaland mentioned. “They play amazing football. All the pressure, we have to deliver on the major stage and that’s what we did. We controlled the whole first half, created chances.”.

According to recent reports, for Maresca, the victory was also a challenge against Porto’s aggression, with the Italian coach adding: “I was very pleased. We know in this kind of game when you come here it’s always difficult or tricky. The environment, the way they grew up, it’s normal, but I think we dealt with that very good.”.

Top performance, Enzo 👊✨ pic.twitter.com/ds0f207tpS.

September 13: Manchester United vs Manchester City (Premier League)September 17: Manchester City vs Norwich (League Cup)September 20: Manchester City vs Sunderland (Premier League)October 11: Liverpool vs Manchester City (Premier League)October 14: Manchester City vs PSG (Champions League).

Man City have now won seven of their last eight opening matchdays in the UEFA Champions League 🔵Starting strong 💪 pic.twitter.com/CIjsMj4Dig.

“I think we could have scored more goals, especially in the first half. We overall deserved the win and happy with the performance. If you think you can come to a place like this and play and not concede any chances, that is not realistic and it is normal. I am quite lucky as I have a squad of good players. It is a special competition and all the games are very difficult. He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] never panicked and was very good. The performance from him was unbelievable. I am happy to reunite with Enzo [Fernandez], who was very good.”.

36 - Erling Haaland scored his 36th UEFA Champions League goal for Manchester City, equalling Sergio Agüero as joint-most for the Citizens in the competition.Inevitability. pic.twitter.com/HHbNadybxh.

It has been revealed that “I am so happy with how my teammates have welcomed me into the club. They are not just great players but great human beings. The fans have been absolutely brilliant and this is a new step in my career. Erling [Haaland] is an animal, a beast. Every time I am on the pitch, I will look for him and look to assist him. He is an amazing human being and helped me settle in. I am happy Enzo [Maresca] did all he good to make the move happen. I am so grateful for everything he has done for me and my family.”.

5️⃣9️⃣ appearances 5️⃣9️⃣ goals@Erling's #UCL record 🤯 pic.twitter.com/v6IvpwC9vm.

“Amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it was going to be a tough game, they play amazing football. We had to deliver on the biggest stage and we did. We controlled the whole of the first half. We created a lot of chances. They pushed us for a good 25 minutes in the second half but we pulled through. These are the games we have to win. We have had a great start to the season.

“He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] had a really good game and he has been amazing in training. I think we have a gem there. We have to learn and Enzo [Maresca] demands a lot from us. We demand a lot from each other. It was an unreal atmosphere so I hope Enzo is happy with that.”.

The final whistle is blown and Manchester City begin their Champions League campaign with a 2-0 win in Porto. Erling Haaland’s double gives Enzo Maresca a victory in his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City.

Industry observers note that enzo has two shots from range in quick succession, one from a free-kick. The free-kick goes just wide and the second is saved by D Costa.

It has been an ill-tempered game and tempers have boiled over again. Rosario and Haaland are involved in a tussle on the floor, which then leads to a mass melee. Haaland and Rosario are both booked for their part in starting that. Haaland is pleased that he got booked but I am not sure why. Both played their part in that melee.

According to recent reports, enzo Maresca’s side will head home with all three points. Ait-Nouri’s cross from the left side of the box picks out Haaland, who first-time shot from 10 yards out picks out the far corner. A clinical finish from Haaland and Manchester City will start their Champions League campaign with a win.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw.

There will be five added minutes.

That is really poor refereeing. Porto are denied two clear fouls before Rosario is then punished for a foul on Enzo, which was a foul but so too were the previous two incidents. Francesco Farioli is then booked for his protestations but you can understand their frustration.

Ait-Nouri has the chance to warp up the three points with an effort from the edge of the box but his shot with his weaker right foot goes narrowly wide.

Nothing comes from the corner as Hwang’s delivery to the front post is dreadful.

Haaland has his fourth headed chance of the game but this one goes over the bar from Ndiaye’s cross. Haaland has scored one of those chances but spurned some good ones.

Down the other end, Fofana, only just on, wins Porto a corner and whips up the home fans.

According to recent reports, A final change of the night for Porto sees Fofana replace Veiga. One last roll of the dice from Francisco Farioli.

Whilst Manchester City’s lead is only 1-0, Porto will believe an equaliser is there for them. However, the momentum they were building 10/15 minutes ago has seemingly been lost and the visitors have managed to wrestle back a bit more control.

Industry observers note that that is a substantial chance missed by Pepe. Gimenez receives it down the left and pings a cross to the back post. The cross perfectly picks out Pepe, who fluffs his lines and completely mis-kicks.

Manchester City are making their final two substitutions of the night as Kovacic and Ait-Nouri come on for Bouaddi and Foden. Ait-Nouri looks like he is going to play left wing.

Two more changes for Porto as Silva and M Fernandes are replaced by Gimenez and Moura.

Recent findings suggest that porto are going to make their first two changes of the night as Hwang and former Norwich man Sainz come on. Varela and Gomes head off.

According to recent reports, for the second time in the half, Donnarumma is lucky. To be fair to the Manchester City keeper, the pass back to him is poor but he is then fortunate. His attempted ball out to his left is intercepted by Gomes but it rolls behind for a goal kick. That ball could have rolled straight into the Manchester City net or fallen straight back at Gomes feet with an empty net ahead of him. Donnarumma was very lucky on Saturday against Coventry to avoid a calamitous moment and he is lucky to avoid another awful moment for the second time in quick succession.

Industry observers note that man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn.

It has been revealed that ndiaye receives it out on the left before driving inside. He gets his shot away from the edge of the box and tries to pick out the far corner but it is too close to D Costa and an easy save for the Porto keeper.

Recent findings suggest that A fine pass from Rosario inside his own half cuts through Manchester City’s midfield sends Varela racing through the Manchester City half. He plays it out to his right to find Gomes, who cuts inside onto his left before trying to beat Donnarumma at his near post but the shot goes wide.

Industry observers note that enzo Maresca responds to a shift in momentum in this game making a double change. Anderson and Ndiaye come on for Cherki and Semenyo.

Porto have started to gain some momentum and they want a penalty. Bouaddi is perhaps a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul right on the edge of the box but it may have been just outside the penalty area. You can feel the game starting to turn in Porto’s favour.

According to recent reports, varela is inches away from an equaliser for Porto and plenty of the home fans thought the ball was in the net. Varela sends a curling effort towards goal from the edge of the box but it goes narrowly wide.

It has been revealed that that was a glorious chance for Porto to equalise. A corner is sent in from the left to the back post, where Alberto heads it back across goal. However, none of his teammates, including Silva, could tap the ball into the net. Porto should probably be back on level terms.

Sources indicate that donnrumma is a very, very lucky man. Porto would have had a certain penalty as Donnarumma completely flattened Pepe but the latter was offside so it is no penalty. Donnarumma has been booked but avoids a penalty, which would have been a guarantee had Pepe been onside.

According to recent reports, just three minutes into the second half, Enzo Maresca has made a substitution. Gvardiol, on a yellow, is withdrawn and Khusanov is brought on.

Recent findings suggest that porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was embracing Daniel Sturridge in the press box and they weren’t in their seats when the goal went in. Lovely move from City and Haaland steered in his 58th goal in the competition.

Erling Haaland moves 7th in the ALL-TIME UCL top-scorers list 💪🇳🇴📊 pic.twitter.com/oIkrPxm0gT.

Haaland wasted two headed opportunities in the first half but he does not spurn this chance. It is a first Manchester City assist for Enzo, who clips in a cross from the left side of the box. Haaland meets it and his header glances off the far post and goes in.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s.

It has been revealed that gabriel Clarke on Amazon Prime has reported that there was some trouble in the tunnel as the two sides went off for half-time. Both sets of security teams for the clubs were forced to step in.

We are back under way in Porto. Tempers were really starting to boil over as that first half wore on so will that continue into the second half?

Sources indicate that the former Liverpool, Manchester City and Chelsea striker has described the incident involving Marc Guehi and Gabri Veiga as a “nasty collision” and “it does not look good at all”. I think Guehi is a lucky man to still be on the pitch as some VAR officials would surely have recommended a review for that foul. Porto boss Francesco Farioli felt Guehi led with his elbow and the home fans were not happy with that as well as a number of other decisions in that first half.
