All the stats are massively in Manchester City’s favour but the key statistic, the scoreline, remains level.

It has been revealed that the first half is brought to an end and tempers are flaring as the two sides head off, with the game level at 0-0 at the break. The Porto fans and players are not happy with the officiating and Enzo is also involved in some antics.

It has been revealed that gvardiol needs to be careful as he is not punished for delaying a restart when you consider he is already on a booking. The Porto fans want to see a second yellow but the referee states the ball was moving so Porto could not take the restart.

Three added minutes to conclude this first half.

Industry observers note that should Guehi be in trouble here? He appears in real time to win his header but when you watch the replays he led with his arm. He catches Veiga right in the face and Guehi could be in some strife. However, VAR is not going to take any further action and Guehi can count himself lucky. The medics are on to tend to Veiga and you do wonder why VAR has not recommended a review. The ridiculous thing about that was that Guehi was not punished with a yellow card or even a free-kick. That clearly shows the referee did not properly see it.

Sources indicate that porto fans quick to remind Ruben Dias and Enzo Fernandez of their Benfica history. They jeered the pair when they got on the ball. Enzo is getting it from all angles at the moment, with Coventry fans taunting him at the weekend. He can expect more of that in the Premier League after his part in England’s exit at the World Cup, which led to Argentina players holding up a flag saying the Falkland Islands were Argentina’s.

In a recent development, tensions are boiling over. They have been threatening to do so between Gomes and Gvardiol for a little while and now they do. Gomes steals the ball off Gvardiol and attempts to counter but is pulled back by Gvardiol, who is rightly booked. Gomes is not happy with Gvardiol and they come to blows.

D Costa twice denies Manchester City in a matter of seconds. First he saves from Haaland, then gets to his feet to deny Cherki. Manchester City are knocking on the door and you do feel like a goal is coming for Enzo Maresca’s side.

No goals in Porto but Real Madrid have their second at home against Inter Milan through Fede Valverde.

Manchester City struggled to carve out any genuine chances in the opening quarter of an hour but there are creating more and more opportunities, the latest falling to Foden, whose shot from the right side of the box looking for the far corner is saved by D Costa.

It has been revealed that it is not often you see Haaland miss two good chances with his head in quick succession but that is what has happened. Semenyo cuts inside on the left onto his right and curls in a cross into a good area. He picks out Haaland but the Norwegian’s header misses the target. He knows he should have done better as he shakes his head in frustration.

Porto’s front three have struggled to have much of an impact in the game, in particular Silva up top, who has been almost non-existent.

A great save from D Costa to deny Haaland. Foden’s cross just before the byline on the left side of the box picks out Haaland. The Norwegian has barely touched the ball tonight but comes close to opening the scoring. However, D Costa is on hand to deny him with a fine save. Should Haaland have given D Costa the chance to save it? Maybe not.

Diogo Costa CLAWS away Erling Haaland's header 🧤Man City come closest so far in Porto 👀 pic.twitter.com/KVnBHdbNlH.

In a recent development, in probably the marquee match-up of the night, Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid are taking on Inter Milan at the Bernabeu. Real have just taken the lead through Kylian Mbappe.

It has been revealed that semenyo cuts inside from the left and gets a shot away from the edge of the box but it is straight at D Costa. That was Manchester City’s first shot of the night.

It has been revealed that veiga has a shot saved at the near post by Donnarumma but the offside flag goes up. Veiga and Pep exchange a neat one-two down Porto’s left before Veiga’s effort is saved but Pepe was offside in the build-up.

Recent findings suggest that manchester City are dominating possession and perhaps it was a ploy by Enzo Marecsa to take it slowly and hog the ball in order to take the early sting out of Porto. The visitors would have been expecting the hosts would want to start hot so maybe they were willing to be slow on the ball in order to quieten down the crowd early doors. They have not had a shot yet and not really threatened the Porto goal but the hosts have not offered much going forward.

The weather in Porto really is horrible, the type of weather you would expect in Manchester in mid-November than Porto in early September.

Porto have a strong defensive record thus far this season but undoubtedly they will be tested a lot more tonight than they are in Liga Portugal. You would also imagine they will have to be clinical in attack as they are unlikely to create as many chances as they do domestically.

Sources indicate that with it hammering down, Porto boss Francesco Farioli has swapped his lovely suit that he was wearing pre-game for a tracksuit top and cap. At half-time, he will probably head back in drenched like all the players if he is active in his dugout.

We are under way at the Estádio do Dragão with the rain still teaming down in Porto. Manchester City’s Champions League campaign gets going.

In a recent development, it has been pouring down in Porto but that has not dampened the spirits of the home fans, who are in fine voice ahead of kick-off. The pyrotechnics have gone off and it is loud inside the Dragão. Both sides then emerge from the tunnel and here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:.

In a recent development, it has been a decent day for Phil Foden already. The City forward’s race horse, Wreck It Ronnie, won at Goodwood and set a newly introduced record in the sport. The horse named after his son defeated Najidi Storm, which was started the race with 1-33 odds. It means the favourite is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. Foden’s family also call him “Ronnie”, which is the name he gave his son.

The referee tonight in Porto is Szymon Marciniak, which may not be a good omen considering Manchester City have been knocked out of the Champions League in the last three seasons. The Polish referee was branded a “Madridista” last year after being pictured with a Real wash bag in the dressing room. Barcelona were unhappy with this after he took charge of a clash against Inter Milan which ended in an epic defeat.

Aston Villa have held on to beat Club Brugge 3-2 and you can catch all the reaction to that game right here.

The massive news here at Estádio do Dragão is that Ayyoub Bouaddi is given his full Manchester City debut, after coming off the bench in previous Premier League games. The Morocco midfielder, 18, starts in midfield in place of Elliot Anderson from the team that defeated Coventry at the weekend. Phil Foden is also given the nod, replacing Iliman Ndiaye.

The Opta Supercomputer, before a ball was kicked tonight, has produced these numbers for what it thinks about who might win the Champions League this season:.

The Argentine started for Manchester City on Saturday against Coventry and he once more takes a place in the centre of their midfield tonight. He starts alongside Ayyoub Bouaddi to form a £200m+ starting midfield pairing.

Sources indicate that aston Villa are into the second half of their game over at Club Brugge. As they kicked off in the second half, Villa were 3-1 up but Brugge have got a goal back. It could be a nervy finish for Unai Emery’s side and you can follow the conclusion of that match right here.

In the forward line for Porto tonight is Brazilian winger William Gomes. The 20-year-old joined Porto from Sao Paulo in 2025 and already has four goal involvements (two goals, two assists) to his name in Liga Portugal this season. He was linked with a move to the Premier League over the summer and you would expect will continue to be on the radar of English clubs going forward.

It has been a positive start for Unai Emery’s Aston Villa out in Belgium as they lead Club Brugge 3-1 at half-time.

Industry observers note that enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Sources indicate that manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

“It is a hard place to come [Porto],” said Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that shows a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”.

In a recent development, porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

“We are going to face one of the big favourites to win the competition,” Farioli stated. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”.

Industry observers note that porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

Team news from Portugal to follow shortly.

Si on vous dit Aviron Bayonnais contre Tarbes, vous penserez sûrement à une rencontre de rugby du passé puisque le Stadoceste Tarbais, champion de France en 1973, opère désormais en Fédérale 3, soit le 7ème niveau.

Mais Aviron Bayonnais - Tarbes, c'était une rencontre de football, Nationale 1, qui s'est déroulée samedi soir et qui nous intéresse puisque dans les rangs basques figure un ancien Vert, Jibril Othman. Sur le stade Didier Deschamps, natif de Bayonne, l'Aviron l'a emporté à l'problem d'un match plein de péripéties. Menés 1 à 0 au bout de 10 minutes, à 10 au bout de 20 minutes, avec un blessé au bout de 30 minutes, les Basques ont su renverser la situation pour l'emporter en toute fin de match avec un but de Jibril Othman à la 82ème minute, concluant de l'extérieur du pied droit un centre venu de la droite.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 15:32 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 15:36 EST, 22 November 2026.

Just when they thought they were beginning to make some progress, along comes another embarrassing setback for Hibs and the decision-makers who have led them into this most trying of seasons.

Before the international break, the impression was that their recently-appointed head coach Marink Reedijk had turned a corner with that Premier Sports Cup semi-final victory over Hearts at Hampden and a 4-0 win at Pittodrie.

According to recent reports, well, if he did, it has taken them headlong into another cul-de-sac. That’s how it felt at Easter Road yesterday when they were trounced 4-0 by Dundee United and left second-bottom of the Premiership table with more than a third of the season completed.

It made rather a mockery of the club’s social media channels, the profile pages of which proudly trumpet their newfound status as ‘Premier Sports Cup finalists’… with an exclamation mark and a golden trophy emoji thrown in for good measure.

In a recent development, self-respecting Hibs fans won’t be fooled by the propaganda. Not after a humiliating afternoon on which their much-vaunted anthem, ’Sunshine on Leith’, was belted out by a gleeful away support at Easter Road.

Long before Zac Sapsford’s first-half double and strikes after the interval by Lyall Cameron and Jesse Randall, some supporters were digging out their anti-board banners and using a megaphone to voice their frustration with those upstairs.

Malky Mackay is under growing pressure from supporters in his role as Hibs sporting director.

Zac Sapsford scores the first of Dundee United 's four goals against Hibs at Easter Road.

Dundee boss Steven Pressley says that he alone was to blame for their 8-0 thrashing by Hearts.

Sources indicate that this is how it works at struggling clubs, where fans need someone to blame. First, they target players. Then they single out the manager. When his replacement proves to be no more effective, they have little option but to turn their guns on the board.

Sources indicate that not that there’s anything wrong with holding the hierarchy to account if they are the common denominator in a lengthy period of under-achievement. There has been little sign of progress at Easter Road since Bournemouth owner Bill Foley sold his Hibs shares back to the Gordon family last year, having suggested that they didn’t listen to his input. Substantial questions are also being asked of sporting director Malky Mackay who was asked in 2024 to lead and oversee the entire football operation, including recruitment and the appointment of a head coach.

Club legend David Gray had his moments as manager, but in the end, supporters wanted rid. Reedijk may turn out to be the real deal but the early signs are that he is struggling with the squad he has inherited. Too many of them failed to do the basics yesterday.

Unlike Hibs, Jim Goodwin’s Dundee United are a strong side with a clear identity. Not for nothing have they gone eight games without defeat, but they scored all too easily as they racked up their biggest-ever victory at Easter Road.

Recent findings suggest that hibs’ squad appears to be weak, imbalanced and too full of ill-advised signings for Reedijk to make the kind of impact he would like. The holes in it are such that he recently opted to use Scotland defender Grant Hanley as an emergency centre-forward.

Reedijk needs to begin an overhaul of that playing staff in the January window, but how much power will be granted in that process? The Dutch coach has already hinted that he will not be given the final say when it comes to transfers.

In a recent development, the fans are nervous about another rebuild under Mackay and his recruitment staff, whose work in the summer window left a lot to be desired. Jason Kerr was a double-winner with St Johnstone, but he has cut a hapless figure at the back. Midfielder Azeem Abdulai, signed on a three-year contract from Leyton Orient, has made only four appearances, just one from the start. And then there is striker Nathan Lowe, on loan from Stoke City, who is struggling to adapt.

Mackay’s record is under heavy scrutiny. He is to be commended for making a profit of around £6million on striker Kieron Bowie, but why has there been no substantial replacement since the striker’s move to Italy nearly a year ago? Can he really argue that expensive signings such as Thibault Klidje and Ante Suto have been value for money?

Sources indicate that A club of Hibs’ size, with those resources, should not be in the relegation zone. Nor should they be struggling so pitifully in their own stadium – they have lost nine of their last ten league games there and haven’t taken three points at home since April.

According to recent reports, which tees up nicely Dundee’s visit to Easter Road on Tuesday, not least because the Tayside club suffered a humiliation of their own this weekend. While Hibs were conceding four, Steven Pressley's side were shipping eight in a hammering by Hearts that has surely inflicted significant psychological damage.

It has been revealed that to his great credit, Pressley insisted afterwards that he alone was to blame for his team’s wretched performance. That may have been true on the night, but over an extended period, a club’s fortunes tend to be shaped by decisions off the pitch. As Hibs have been finding out.

THE END GAME? Writing is on the wall for McCann after revitalised Dons ran riot at Rugby Park

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1000 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Let’s face it, Neil McCann was never the most popular of appointments with Kilmarnock fans, but not even his harshest critics could deny that he did a fine job in keeping the club in Scotland’s top flight last season.
  • Unfortunately for him, it looks increasingly likely that he isn’t going to get the chance to repeat the trick this time around.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 18:00 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 18:11 EST, 22 November 2026.

Let’s face it, Neil McCann was never the most popular of appointments with Kilmarnock fans, but not even his harshest critics could deny that he did a fine job in keeping the club in Scotland’s top flight last season.

Unfortunately for him, it looks increasingly likely that he isn’t going to get the chance to repeat the trick this time around.

Recent findings suggest that the writing already appears to be on the wall for the 52-year-old. A question of when, rather than if, he is given his jotters.

By all accounts, he hasn’t lost the dressing room. Which is just as well, because he has well and truly lost the punters, whose collective mood shifted from angry to apathetic over the course of 90-odd thoroughly entertaining minutes at Rugby Park on Saturday.

When that happens, it’s a long way back.

Recent findings suggest that mcCann knows this himself. It is not as if he is operating with the blinkers on.

It's a tough watch for Neil McCann as his Kilmarnock team go down 4-2 to Aberdeen.

His assessment of his team’s performances week-to-week tends to be pretty honest, as it was again this weekend.

The problem is, as he put it, that he is coming across ‘like a broken record’.

According to recent reports, his team are hopeless at the back and toothless up top, with some encouraging stuff in between. If the supporters are sick of hearing it, imagine how scunnered McCann must feel saying it. He certainly looks it.

If they continue to defend like this, relegation is a nailed-on certainty.

In a recent development, they shipped four here — and it could have very easily been a few more — to take their tally to 33 conceded for the season in just 14 games. It’s laughable, there’s no other way to dress it up.

Aberdeen’s Kevin Nisbet scored twice in four first-half minutes, capitalising on a woeful clearance from keeper Nico Mantl to put the Dons ahead, before curling a free-kick straight through the weakest wall you’ve ever seen in your life to double the visitors’ advantage.

Fresh Dons boss Mario Frick can't hide his delight after victory in first game in charge.

The third goal — shortly after Greg Kiltie had given McCann’s men a lifeline — was the worst of the lot. Former Rugby Park skipper Brad Lyons ghosted in behind the completely unaware Michael Schjonning-Larsen to head the ball home after Cathal McCarthy failed to stop Nesta Guinness-Walker’s cross from the left touchline.

Shocking stuff all round, and exactly the type of goal which has killed Killie all season — and will continue to do so until something drastic changes.

Let’s not forget, the recent international break afforded McCann and his staff a fortnight to work on things on the training pitch ahead of what is going to be a gruelling winter schedule.

It has been revealed that while the Killie manager will ultimately be the one to pay the price, his players need to have a right good look at themselves too. There was simply no sign of anyone in that backline taking any sort of responsibility.

Kilmarnock’s next three games are against St Mirren, Hibernian and Motherwell — the three sides currently directly above them in the table.

According to recent reports, an absolute minimum of four points from that run is required, otherwise this is going to get rather ugly. In truth, defeat in Paisley this weekend may well be the final nail in McCann’s coffin.

On the other hand, things are finally starting to look up for the Dons.

New manager Mario Frick has promised to bring heavy metal football to these shores, and if Saturday is anything to go by, the ex-Liechtenstein international is a man of his word.

McCann's job looks to be on the line after bottom club Killie succumbed to another defeat.

His team were a joy to watch going forward here, particularly in the first half.

It was a million miles away from the kind of turgid football offered up under his predecessor as Dons manager, Stephen Robinson.

Speed, intensity, aggression, quality. The performance was full of it.

You could count the number of times the Dons faffed about with the ball on one hand. Every time there was an opportunity to get forward, they took it.

Ante Palaversa, making his first appearance of the campaign, was at the heart of it.

For whatever reason, Robinson never fancied the Croatian, a stance which perplexed the Pittodrie faithful. Indeed, the 26-year-old — once on the books of Manchester City — was deemed surplus to requirements over the summer.

The Dons will be delighted there were no takers.

It has been revealed that he was outstanding here as he commanded that space between midfield and defence without breaking sweat. Nobody in Killie colours could get near him.

Both Nicky Devlin and Guinness-Walker bombed up their respective wings all day, while some of the link-up play between Nisbet — who should have had a hat-trick before Findlay Marshall wrapped things up late on — and Hicham Mahou was delightful.

Defensively, they were all over the shop at times, and no doubt they will be punished heavily at Ibrox on Tuesday night if they are as open as this.

But this was a display to simply be enjoyed rather than picked apart. It makes a change.

It has been revealed that KILMARNOCK (4-2-3-1): Mantl 3; McCarthy 4, Kamson-Kamara 3 (Brandon 46), Stanger 4, Schjonning-Larsen 4; Lowery 6, Tshibola 5 (McKenzie 85); Ring 3 (O’Hara 46), Kiltie 6 (Clescenco 83), Hugill 5.5; Owen 4 (John-Jules 54). Booked: Owen, Hugill. Manager: Neil McCann 3.

ABERDEEN (4-1-3-2): Muller 5; Devlin 6, Molloy 6, Milne 6, Guinness- Walker 7; PALAVERSA 8 (Aremu 61); Lyons 7, Briedl 7 (Mouloula 61), Armstrong 6.5 (Marshall 71); Mahou 6 (Smith 80), Nisbet 8. Booked: None. Manager: Mario Frick 7.

  • Recent findings suggest that nous sommes un club patrimonial, une institution du football européen.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that directeur général adjoint de l'ASSE en charge de la marque, du marketing et de la communication, Cédric Chambaz s'exprime dans le hors série de Décideurs Corporate Finances. Extraits.

"Il y a un changement macroéconomique dans l’industrie du football. L’ère du chef d’entreprise qui veut s’offrir une danseuse en investissant ses fonds propres pour se faire plaisir le week-end est derrière nous. Aujourd’hui, nous sommes dans une logique d’investissement beaucoup plus raisonnée, même si elle laisse toute sa place à la passion. Quand Larry Tannenbaum mandate Ivan Gazidis pour trouver un club de football dans lequel investir, il recherche un actif à fort potentiel sur un marché mûr. Il ne s’agit donc pas du tout de mécénat à fonds perdus. Pour autant, cet investissement porte sur un produit d’émotion, et l’AS Saint-Étienne dispose d’atouts considérables en la matière.

Recent findings suggest that nous sommes un club patrimonial, une institution du football européen. Historiquement, nous sommes une des équipes les plus titrées de France et nous bénéficions d’un engouement qui dépasse largement notre territoire. Nos supporters sont répartis dans toute la France et notre fréquentation au stade est totalement décorrélée de notre niveau sportif actuel. Nous affichons la sixième affluence du football français, alors que nous évoluons sportivement en deuxième division.

In a recent development, pour Kilmer Sport Ventures, l’ASSE présentait des caractéristiques intéressantes mais le club était aussi une sorte de géant endormi qui, ces dernières années, n’avait pas bénéficié des investissements de modernisation nécessaires pour rester compétitif dans le football contemporain. L’idée est donc de réveiller le club grâce à des investissements ciblés, fondés sur une analyse approfondie de l’existant et de nos objectifs afin de repositionner l’AS Saint-Étienne comme une institution, sur le terrain comme en dehors.

In a recent development, un club de football peut être considéré comme un média. Plus son exposition est forte, dans les médias traditionnels comme sur les réseaux sociaux, plus il peut valoriser son inventaire commercial, c’est-à-dire les espaces qu’il propose à ses sponsors. À l’ASSE, nous bénéficions d’une audience nationale élevée. C’est ce qui nous rend attractifs pour le diffuseur, même en Ligue 2. Nous travaillons aussi à valoriser cette audience sur les réseaux sociaux, où nous rassemblons plus de 2,9 millions de fans sur l’ensemble de nos plateformes.

Recent findings suggest that aujourd’hui, nous sommes capables de générer en France l’une des 10 plus fortes valorisations médiatiques pour nos annonceurs, et ce malgré notre présence en deuxième division. C’est notamment le fruit du travail mené en communication et en marketing pour faire rayonner l’équipe au-delà du stade.

L’enjeu, au-delà de la seule billetterie, est de transformer notre notoriété en revenus. Cela passe d’abord par notre ancrage régional. Nous devons continuer à attirer des supporters au stade et à remplir Geoffroy-Guichard. Mais nous devons aussi toucher ceux qui ne peuvent pas venir au stade, en développant notre marque et nos produits dérivés. Cela suppose de travailler notre présence sur les réseaux sociaux, de valoriser les joueurs et de construire leur image, notamment lorsqu’ils sont issus de notre centre de formation. Certains disposent déjà de communautés importantes, capables de contribuer à la vente de maillots et d’ouvrir de nouveaux marchés. À défaut, c’est au club de construire cette visibilité.

In a recent development, notre ambition est de conquérir de nouveaux publics, notamment en Europe, mais chaque chose en son temps. Notre audience dépasse aujourd’hui notre territoire régional, mais nous ne pouvons pas prétendre rivaliser aujourd’hui avec le PSG à l’échelle internationale. Cela passera d’abord par le retour en Ligue 1 et par des performances sportives à la hauteur de nos ambitions. C’est toute la complexité de notre activité. Nous pouvons bâtir une stratégie marketing solide et développer nos outils de fidélisation, mais les résultats sportifs restent déterminants. Si vous perdez cinq matchs de suite, la dynamique commerciale s’en ressent forcément. Le projet sportif reste le juge de paix, même si nous devons apprendre à développer nos revenus au-delà du seul résultat du week-end.

Industry observers note that la grande différence entre être DAF ou CMO d’une start-up dans la tech et dans un club comme Saint-Etienne ? A mon sens, elle tient à l’attachement des supporters envers le club et à la manière dont il influence leur vie. Très peu d’entreprises peuvent se targuer de voir leur logo tatoué sur le corps d’un de leurs clients et, pourtant, c’est le cas de l’ASSE. En outre, lorsqu’on se promène dans la ville, tous les acteurs économiques et politiques ont un avis sur la situation du club. Dans une région industrielle en difficulté, cette proximité et l’intensité de cette relation sont primordiales pour rassembler la population. Cette intensité m’a vraiment surpris, par comparaison avec les autres entreprises où j’ai travaillé. Le club cristallise des espoirs, des projections de succès qui transcendent le football.".

Tech Report: Dual passports issue continues to plague Dutch-based footballers

  • Dutch-born footballers who were called up to play for former colonies such as Suriname and Indonesia are still in limbo over their national status, six months after the “passportgate” crisis first flared up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Dutch-born footballers who were called up to play for former colonies such as Suriname and Indonesia are still in limbo over their national status, six months after the “passportgate” crisis first flared up.

Suriname’s parliament passed a law in September enabling players who are selected for the national team to gain citizenship automatically.

But the Dutch immigration service IND said the law passed in Suriname made no difference to the rules on dual nationality in the Netherlands.

“The fact that Surinamese nationality has been obtained by legal means is not enough on its own to qualify for one of the exceptional categories under our law,” a spokesman for the Dutch justice ministry told broadcaster NOS.

The law was intended to settle the question of dual nationality for footballers, which arose last March when NAC Breda challenged the eligibility of Go Ahead Eagles defender Dean James.

James took Indonesian citizenship last year after accepting an invitation to play for the national team, but under Dutch dual nationality rules he was required to give up his original passport.

It has been revealed that the Dutch football association KNVB launched an investigation into the employment status of players who were called up by countries such as Suriname, Cape Verde and Indonesia. In the meantime it arranged for Dutch-based players to be given temporary work permits so they could keep playing for their clubs.

Losing Dutch nationality also stripped them of their EU citizenship, meaning they would need to obtain visas and meet stricter criteria, such as an annual salary threshold of €600,000, to be eligible to play in the Eredivisie.

Several players have passed up invitations to join the Surinamese squad because of the uncertainty, including Danilho Doekhi of Lazio, Milan van Ewijk of Coventry City and Jayden Oosterwolde of Fenerbahçe.

National team manager Henk Fraser mentioned it was “inexplicable” that players’ livelihoods were being damaged by their desire to play international football.

In a recent development, “Both countries have to get together and clarify the situation,” he told NOS. “This is a straightforward case of people following their hearts and wanting to play for Suriname, but not knowing where they stand.”.

Some players remarked they felt misled by the Surinamese football association, which told them they were playing for the national team on “sports passports” that allowed them to remain Dutch citizens.

Former Feyenoord winger Jean-Paul Boëtius said he only discovered after he was first called up for Suriname last year that he had inadvertently renounced his Dutch citizenship as a result.

Shortly afterwards he received a letter from the city council in Rotterdam telling him to hand in his Dutch passport, which he had recently renewed, because it was no longer valid.

Industry observers note that “I now have a sticker in my Surinamese passport that says I have a residency permit allowing me to live in the Netherlands,” he told NOS. “But that’s only for a year. It’s a very difficult situation. I want to become Dutch again. I was born and brought up here.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • "Je suis arrivé en 2014 à Saint-Etienne.
  • According to recent reports, C’est le seul club qui est venu me chercher, Saint-Etienne.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Défenseur de Chelsea, 8e de Premier League à 12 points du leader Arsenal de son ex-acolyte stéphanois William Saliba (remis de sa blessure au dos et pressenti pour jouer son premier match de la saison ce dimanche lors du choc contre Manchester City), Wesley Fofana est revenu hier sur ses vertes années dans Zack en roue libre. Extraits.

"Je suis arrivé en 2014 à Saint-Etienne. J’ai découvert la région, les Stéphanois. Le Forez… qu’est-ce qu’il fait froid là-bas ! C’est dur, la ville c’est compliqué. Tu peux entendre beaucoup de personnes te dire qu’il n’y a rien à faire dans cette ville, que c’est moche, etc. Mais moi j’ai bien aimé Saint-Etienne ! C’est sûr qu’il n’y a pas grand-chose à faire, que tu ne vas pas t’amuser comme si t’étais à Lyon, à Paris ou à Marseille. Mais il y a un p’tit truc, une histoire de fou et tu t’attaches à cette ville. Franchement, j’ai vécu de belles années là-bas ! A Marseille, il y a tellement une histoire forte que quand tu vas parler avec les gens, ils sont fiers de te parler de la ville. C’est beau. Sainté, c’est un peu similaire. Avec le froid en plus mais franchement c’est une superbe ville.

According to recent reports, C’est le seul club qui est venu me chercher, Saint-Etienne. Je jouais dans un club très populaire à Marseille qui s'appelle le Sporting Club Air Bel, et il y avait tout le temps des recruteurs car c'est un club qui est connu pour sortir des joueurs pour conduire en centre de formation. J'ai fait beaucoup d'essais, dans presque tous les clubs de France, à part le PSG et les clubs dans le Nord. J’ai fait des essais à Montpellier, Nice, Monaco, Toulouse, Bordeaux, Marseille. J'ai même fait Auxerre. Lyon ? Non. Quand t'es petit, pour aller à Lyon, il faut savoir jouer au ballon. Moi, j'étais trop un boucher !

La première fois que j'ai fait un essai à Saint-Etienne, ils ne m'ont pas pris à la base, ils m'ont dit, « on va te revoir », la fameuse phrase « On te rappellera. » Mais ils sont revenus me voir quand je jouais avec Air Bel, et ils m'ont refait faire un essai. Et après cet essai, ils m'ont dit :  « c'est bon, on va te garder ». Quand j’arrive là-bas, c'est compliqué. En fait, t'arrives et il y a des règles, des codes, des trucs que tu ne peux pas faire. Et moi, quand j'étais petit, c'était un peu : si je veux faire un truc, je veux le faire. Et d'où je viens, il n'y a pas réellement... Ce n'est pas qu'il n'y a pas de règles, parce que ce ne serait pas bien de dire qu'il n'y a pas de règles. Parce que j'ai été éduqué, j'ai eu une bonne éducation, mais ce n'est pas pareil. Les règles, tu peux les contourner. Pour nous, les règles, si on n'est pas d'accord avec la règle, on va la contourner. Un peu de filouterie, voilà.

Sources indicate that sauf qu'au centre de formation, ça ne passe pas. Et après, t'arrives, t'es dans un centre avec d'autres jeunes, des gens de ton âge, des gens qui jouent à ta place. Et c'est un peu la « guerre » parce qu'il y a des gens qui jouent à ta place, mais toi, t'es là, tu les regardes, t'as envie de jouer. C'est la concurrence, c'est comme ça. Mais oui, c'était un peu compliqué. Surtout, je quittais Marseille, j'arrivais à Saint-Etienne. Au début, je me suis dit « Mais qu'est-ce que je fous ici ? Qu'est-ce que je vais faire dans cette ville de fous ? » Un truc tout bête, tu sors dehors, c'est où qu'on peut aller grailler, c'est où qu'on peut aller manger ? Tu regardes les grecs, les snacks, il n'y a rien qui va. Tu veux aller te faire couper les cheveux, il n'y a rien qui va. Mais après, petit à petit, tu trouves les petites adresses, les connexions et j’étais bien. Tu rencontres des Stéphanois là-bas, ils te disent « T'inquiète, va ici, va là ».

Sources indicate that franchement, au centre de formation, il y avait du niveau. Je pense qu'il y avait des jeunes en U17, U19, même en réserve, qui étaient « destinés » à du très, très haut niveau, mais qui n'ont jamais réussi à aller le chercher. Après, les Stéphanois, ils sont très fiers et ils ont des grosses valeurs. C'est ça, surtout, qu'on nous a appris. La valeur que le club, il a dans la ville, ça, on le comprend très jeune. Parce que les gens de là-bas, ils vivaient un peu à travers le club. Quand ça gagne le week-end, ils sont très contents. Quand ça perd, ils sont un peu tristes. Et dans la ville, tu le ressens. Le centre de formation, ce n’est que des bons souvenirs. On a fait beaucoup de bêtises, les directeurs du centre voulaient notre peau plus d'une fois. On va dire qu'ils ont des anecdotes. C'est des super souvenirs et on avait de belles générations. Franchement, moi, j'ai connu 98-99, ma génération 2000, 2001, 2002. Franchement, il y a eu des gros joueurs qui sont sortis. Il y a eu de très, très beaux joueurs.

C’est là que j’ai connu William Saliba. On  joué ensemble de U17 jusqu'à U19. On a gagné la Gambardella ensemble. Ouais, j'allais en parler. Même si il n'a pas joué la finale, on a gagné la Gambardella parce qu'on a joué la compétition ensemble. Et après, on a joué pendant un an, un an et demi ensemble. Lui, il est monté très vite en pro. On a joué en pro ensemble. Avec William, c'est une belle histoire parce qu'on a commencé très, très jeunes et on s'est retrouvés en pro ensemble. On a grandi ensemble et on est toujours en contacts même si on joue dans des clubs rivaux. Je le connais par cœur, il me connait par cœur. C'est la famille. On n'a pas besoin de se parler tous les jours mais on va se parler de temps en temps. On va se parler et après, quand on se voit, il n'y a rien qui bouge. C’est beau qu’on ait gardé ça. Parce qu'au-delà du fait qu'on ait grandi ensemble, qu'on soit arrivé au « sommet » ensemble, on joue au même poste. Ça aurait pu affecter notre relation mais depuis jeune, ça n'a jamais touché notre relation. On n'a jamais été affecté par ça, par la concurrence. Même quand on est arrivé en pro, il y a eu beaucoup de trucs qui nous ont mis en compétition, etc. Mais nous, ça ne nous a jamais rien fait. On s'en foutait. Nous, on voulait jouer ensemble, on voulait s'amuser et on voulait le meilleur pour l'autre,.

Quand tu gagnes la Gambardella, t'es un peu la meilleure équipe de jeunes de France. Donc, c'était déjà quelque chose d'incroyable. Au lendemain de notre sacre en Gambardella, on fait un tour d'honneur à Geoffroy-Guichard. Je n'ai jamais fait de banc en pro à ce moment-là, rien ! On fait un tour d'honneur et trois semaines après, je suis sur le banc et il y a une blessure. Et le coach se retourne vers moi et il me fait rentrer arrière-droit contre Alain Saint-Maximin. La première chose que tu as en tête, c'est « il va me salir ». Parce qu'Allan, il est connu pour dribbler, pour salir les gens. Mais après, franchement, sur le moment, je rentre et moi, j'ai qu'un truc en tête, je me dis que chaque fois qu'il touche la balle, il faut que je le monte en l'air. Juste avant de rentrer, je vois l’entraîneur de Nice Patrick Vieira qui fait un geste demandant à ses joueurs d’attaquer de mon côté. Ça te met une petite bouffée de pression. Mais mon coach - enfin, c'était l'adjoint à ce moment-là -  m’a glissé deux ou trois mots avant de rentrer. Julien Sablé m’a dit : « tu joue simple, agressif, tu n’inventes rien , fais ce que tu sais faire. Tu castagnes, tu te bats, tu mets des tacles, des tampons. ». Je n’avais que ça en tête, simple, agressif. Ça s'est bien passé. Bon match, 3-0, première entrée, clean sheet.

It has been revealed that J’enchaîne la semaine d'après, c'est le dernier match de la saison, à Angers. Ma première titu. C’était facile car il n'y avait plus rien à jouer pour les deux équipes. C’était un super match, j’ai kiffé. C'était Jean-Louis Gasset, le coach. Tout le monde le connaît, c'est un mec simple. Et c'était une personne incroyable. J'ai appris beaucoup, beaucoup avec lui et avec son staff. Je n’en garde que de bons souvenirs. C'est sûr que je ne l'ai pas connu aussi longtemps que je l'aurais espéré parce que je n'étais pas réellement avec les pros. Je m'entraînais, mais je n'étais pas réellement avec eux. Ma première apparition en pro j’ai joué latéral mais franchement, je déteste ce poste. Après, comme je l'ai toujours dit, en vrai, tu ne décides pas trop. Tu vas jouer, surtout à cet âge-là, où on va te mettre. Qu'est-ce que tu veux dire ? Tu joues en pro, c’est déjà bien. Sois content, joue tes matchs, fais ton job et après, tu verras. Après, quand tu auras acquis de l'expérience, que  tu auras joué des matchs, tu pourras dire « moi, je préfère, je préfère ci, je préfère ça ». Quand tu es jeune, tu joues où on te met. On m'aurait même mis à gauche ou gardien, c'est bon, j’y serais allé.

Je ne l'avais pas en moi, cette qualité de relance mais ça compte, surtout dans le football de maintenant. Ça compte de fou, ça compte énormément. Jouer au ballon, je n'avais pas ça en moi. C'est mon coach, Julien Sablé, que j'ai eu à Saint-Etienne qui m’a fait travailler ça. C'est lui qui m'a rendu fou et qui a pris des heures et des heures avec moi à me dire qu'il faut que la passe soit comme ça, qu'elle soit claquée, qu'il faut jouer dans ces intervalles-là. C'est lui qui m'a expliqué tout ça. Moi, à la base, moi, en tant que défenseur, mon job, et vraiment, j'ai grandi comme ça, c'était : « tu défends, te ne prends pas de but. On s'en fout à qui tu fais la passe. Quand tu as la balle dans les pieds, tu donnes à ton 6, ton arrière-droit. Ils se débrouillent. Eux, c'est leur job de faire le jeu, de s'amuser avec le ballon. » Moi mon plaisir c'était les tampons, les tacles, gagner mes duels, notamment de la tête. Et c'est après, petit à petit, en faisant des séances, des vidéos, etc., en prenant du temps sur le terrain, petit à petit que j'ai commencé à apprécier cet aspect du foot avec le ballon, et j'ai compris beaucoup de choses.

J’ai fait ma première année en pro dans une équipe qui subissait et prenait beaucoup de buts. Tu subis beaucoup, donc tu défends beaucoup, tu es beaucoup exposé. En tant que défenseur, quand tu es jeune et que tu es beaucoup exposé et que tu défends beaucoup, on parle plus de toi, on te voit plus. Par exemple, on allait plus parler de moi qu'on allait parler des attaquants. Parce qu'on ne faisait que défendre et qu’on ne marquait pas beaucoup de buts. Et même quand on en prenait des buts, c'était souvent, « heureusement qu'il est là, sinon on en aurait pris plus ». Mais d'un autre côté, quand tu es défenseur et que ton équipe prend beaucoup de buts, tu passes des mauvais matchs, tu passes des mauvaises soirées. Tu vas jouer à l'extérieur, tu rentres chez toi, t'en as pris trois. Domicile, le week-end d'après, tu reçois, t'es as pris deux. Tu enchaînes les défaites, t’en prends 4, tu perds 5-1. C'est chaud, ce n'est pas un plaisir. Mais d'un autre côté, quand tu n'en prends pas, c'est multiplié fois 20 comparé à d'autres défenseurs ou à d'autres équipes du championnat. Franchement, c'était dur. Mais d'un autre côté, vu que tu défends beaucoup, tu es exposé pour un défenseur et à mon âge, c'était tout bénef pour moi.

Sources indicate that je fais cette finale de Coupe de France contre le PSG. Je fais un très bon match, mais malheureusement on perd la finale. Après cette finale, il y a un peu tout qui s'accélère. Il y a beaucoup de clubs qui s’intéressent à moi. Franchement, Leicester n’était pas là au début. Pour dire la vérité, à la base, moi, c'est Milan AC. Il y a un appel avec les dirigeants, avec Maldini. Maldini, c'est stylé. Quand il te parle et te dit « je vais te prendre sous mon aile » , j’ai envie de lui dire  « emmène-moi, je signe ce que tu veux. » Au départ, avec mes agents et tout mon entourage, on penche plutôt pour le Milan AC.

Recent findings suggest that après, ça ne se fait pas avec Saint-Etienne parce que d'un côté, Saint-Etienne ne voulait pas me vendre. Mais d'un autre côté, ils étaient un peu dans l'obligation de me vendre par rapport à des problèmes d'argent, etc. Ils étaient un peu entre deux. Ils essaient un peu de faire remonter les enchères. On sait comment ça marche. Milan a monté jusqu'à une limite où ils ont dit « Ça ne sera plus possible. » Et il y a Leicester qui s'est ramené. Leicester, ça a été tout droit. J'ai parlé avec le coach, j'ai parlé avec Kolo Touré qui était dans le staff. Son discours m’a rassuré et mis en confiance. Ensuite, ce n’était pas compliqué. Leicester a fait une offre. Saint-Etienne était d'accord, mais après il y a eu ce problème avec Claude Puel, qui ne voulait vraiment pas me vendre. Mais au final, pour la santé du club, pour le bien du club, il n'avait pas trop le choix. Donc j’ai filé à Leicester l’avant-dernier jour du mercato.".

Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

📅 09 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5475 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under newly introduced head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.
  • It has been revealed that on the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness.
  • And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under newly introduced head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

It has been revealed that on the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a fresh contract.

Sources indicate that so, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face said it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

It has been revealed that mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W.

There are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he showed during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ newly introduced head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

It has been revealed that for Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A massive European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

“I loved it,” Iraola said, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

Liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo highlighted he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

As does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

Recent findings suggest that there was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

It owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc.

It has been revealed that we knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

It has been revealed that this is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

It has been revealed that atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY.

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

Industry observers note that the question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

Recent findings suggest that “I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. They have been playing together forever. We find another comeback after Nottingham Forest, after Newcastle. We still have this thing to improve in the beginning of the games, but I am happy as we have shown some character. This is the Champions League, you do not have easy games.”.

"You can see he's football mad." ⚽Steven Gerrard on Andoni Iraola's passion and the impact he's making at Liverpool 👏🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M3qKhxt8HE.

According to recent reports, andoni Iraola has been speaking to TNT Sports and has confirmed that it was just cramp for the likes of Bradley Barcola, rather than an injury. Milos Kerkez also went off late with what appears to be just cramp.

Atletico had more possession in the second half but Liverpool were much the better side after the break.

According to recent reports, there is the final whistle at Anfield and Liverpool start their Champions League campaign with a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid. Liverpool did fall behind to Marcos Llorente’s goal but goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister give Andoni Iraola a win in his first Champions League game as a manager.

Victory in MD1 🤩 #UCL pic.twitter.com/SWFFhSudFJ.

First Champions League game. First Champions League win for Andoni Iraola ✅ pic.twitter.com/D3CE6w6V0b.

Koumas is tripped by Le Normand and that should be it.

That is a silly foul from Lookman, with Frimpong inside his own box running back towards his own goal, but Lookman decides to push him in the back.

Just 60 seconds remain at Anfield.

There will be five added minutes.

Liverpool think they have sealed it through Frimpong but the offside flag has gone up. First Munoz cuts onto his right and has a shot saved by Oblak. The ball falls to Frimpong, who slots home but he was clearly offside when Munoz took the initial shot.

Kerkez is right now down with cramp and his night is done. He will be replaced by Tsimikas and Liverpool will make their final change at the same time. Koumas comes on for Isak.

It has been revealed that atletico win a corner but it all stems from sloppy play in the centre of the pitch from Gravenberch. He has had a few sloppy moments since coming on.

The corner is flicked on by Hjulmand but ends up coming to nothing.

It isn’t the headline making performance, by any means, but that shouldn’t dilute the importance of Ronald Araujo’s contribution for Liverpool tonight and, indeed, against Ipswich last Friday. He’s doing what Liverpool wanted him to, providing versatility and leadership in their back four and - more than anything - quality. He hasn’t put a foot wrong.

Atletico win a corner out on the left in front of their travelling supporters. Grimaldo’s outswinger is flicked on by the head of Hancko at the near post but it goes over.

Isak has the chance to potentially seal the victory for Liverpool but Le Normand makes a crucial block. Le Normand has only just come on but already made a couple of defensive actions.

Sources indicate that liverpool win a corner out on the left with the last touch coming off Pubill, who was marking Van Dijk from a free-kick. Szoboszlai’s inswinger is headed away by Le Normand.

Digeo Simeone is making his final two substitutions of the night as Le Normand and Hjulmad replace Romero and Barrios,.

Atletico bring on David, on loan from Juventus, for Baena.

Recent findings suggest that alvarez has a chance inside the Liverpool box but his shot is straight at Alisson. There are some appeals for handball but it hit Munoz from such close range that it is never a penalty.

In a recent development, liverpool are making a substitution as Mac Allister, who scored the goal to put Liverpool in front, is replaced by Gravenberch. Mac Allister, who made some comments in the press conference yesterday about his sadness at not being offered a latest contract, put in a good performance in the centre of Liverpool’s midfield. He was on a booking though so probably sensible to take him off when you can guarantee that the Atletico players would have tried to get him sent off.

According to recent reports, we’ll see what happens in the coming weeks and months but there have been glimmers here with Florian Wirtz looking better than he has done with pace to pass to; if it clicks with him, Bradley Barcola & Alexander Isak it could be exciting but one game must be built on. It’s frustrating that Barcola’s night has ended with what appears to be cramp or tightness in his calf because he was getting more joy than he had done before half-time. The massive challenge for Liverpool, too, is whether they have the nous to see this contest out.

The newly introduced Netherlands boss Xavi is in attendance at Anfield tonight, watching the likes of Van Dijk, Frimpong and Gravenberch, although the latter is still yet to come off the Liverpool bench.

In a recent development, this is a concern for Liverpool. Barcola has gone down and seems to have some pain in his left calf. Is it cramp or an injury? It will be a double change for the home side as Frimpong and Munoz come on. Barcola is given a standing ovation as he goes off and the Liverpool fans will be hoping it is just cramp. Ngumoha also heads off.

In a recent development, diego Simeone is going to make his first two changes of the night. Grimaldo and Lookman come on.

Recent findings suggest that it is all Liverpool as they sense a third goal is there for the taking. Ngumoha does well down Liverpool’s left and pushes it past Pubill, who slides in and takes him down. Pubill is booked. He cannot believe it but I do not know why; a clear foul and yellow card.

In a recent development, that is a stunning strike from the Argentine. The ball falls to the midfielder just outside the box and he hits it first time. He hits the ball so crisply and there is nothing Oblak can do to stop it. Liverpool should have taken the lead through Barcola moments before they do now have the lead for the first time tonight.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W.

Well, that’s one way to prove you might warrant a latest contract. A quite beautiful left footed drive from Alexis Mac Allister gives Liverpool the lead and it has been noticeable thus far in Andoni Iraola’s matches that his team get stronger at the start of the second period. Diego Simeone most wonder how Atleti are losing a game they were controlling but Liverpool’s speed on the break is proving very good at causing chaos.

Barcola should have his first Liverpool goal and the hosts should be ahead but the Frenchman misses the target. It is the perfect counter-attack really from Liverpool and it is Wirtz and Barcola who exchange passes from deep inside their own half all the way to the Atletico penalty area. Barcola drives forward, into the Atletico box, and you think he is going to slot it into the bottom corner but his effort goes just wide. Barcola could and perhaps should have a brace tonight.

Barcola wins the first corner of this second half off Hancko right in front of The Kop. Liverpol take it short before Mac Allister clips the ball in. Araujo meets it and his header is powerful but it is off target.

We are back under way at Anfield. No changes from either side at the break.

The first half at Anfield is brought to an end and it is level at 1-1 at the break. Llorente gave Atletico the lead before Szoboszlai equalised for Liverpool. The home fans let the officials know what they think of their performance in that first half.

One added minute at the end of this first half.

There has been about five minutes of squabbling between the Liverpool and Atletico benches, so much so that Tommy Elphick - Andoni Iraola’s assistant - missed Dominik Szoboszlai score the equaliser. Tensions have only increased after a nasty little challenge from Cristian Romero on Alexander Isak. The half-time whistle might be coming at a good time to defuse the situation but you fancy the walk back to the dressing rooms will be spicy.

The conduct of the Atletico players is frankly embarrassing, not a massive surprise from a Diego Simeone side. Kang goes down clutching his face when there was barely any contact and then, unlike Isak, he does not have to spend a minute off the pitch.

Isak is on the ground, clutching at his knee, after a heavy challenge from Romero. It is a nasty challenge from Romero, who remarkably is neither booked nor penalised. To compound the awful officiating, Isak now has to spend a minute off the pitch owing to the new rules. What do you make of that new rule of the player who is down going off for a minute? Have your say in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Moments after Liverpool equalised, Atletico have a decent opportunity to restore their lead but Baena drags his effort wide from the edge of the box.

Recent findings suggest that moments after Barcola could not take a big chance to equalise for Liverpool, Szoboslzai does. First, Barcola is denied by Oblak. Liverpool keep it alive inside the Atletico box and a simple sensational flick by Aruajo finds Szoboszlai, who finds the bottom corner with a clinical finish. Kerkez has been poor tonight but he deserves credit for his part in that goal as he was the player to initially win it back for Liverpool with a good press.

In a recent development, szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool look like a team that has been out of the Champions League for a couple of years and are only just finding its feet, which seems strange given they missed only one year in the last 10. They have glimmers of promise but they aren’t convincing anyone they will blow Atleti’s house down. One day everything will align for Atleti and they will reach another final. They have an outside chance this year, especially if Julian Alvarez - easily the best player on this pitch - has anything to do with it. Diego Simeone always has class strikers at the top of his team and Alvarez stands comparison with any who have gone before.

Wirtz has a great chance to equalise for Liverpool but his shot on the half volley is saved by Oblak. It would not have mattered anyway had the ball ended up in the net because Isak was offside before crossing for Wirtz.

According to recent reports, some of the officiating tonight has been appalling and the latest example is VAR taking a check on a possible red card for Mac Allister for a foul that is never a red card in a million years. The officials then take an age to give yet another obvious offside and, in the end, the referee gives it rather than the linesman. That really does sum up the officials tonight as the referee should not be the one to give offsides.

In a recent development, alvarez shoots from distance and forces Alisson into a good save diving to his right. There was a suspicion of offside from Simeone in the build-up.

Atletico take it short but Simeone’s shot is blocked by Araujo.

The Anfield faithful are furious. Two fouls in quick succession are not given when they were both clearly fouls. The referee appears to have a different interpretation of body checks and taking people out off the ball than the rest of us.

The Spanish side take the lead at Anfield and it is another goal on this ground for Llorente. Alvarez feeds a through ball to pick out the run of Llorente, who is onside. He takes one touch before firing past Alisson from the edge of the box. That is poor, poor defending from Kerkez, who not only played Llorente onside but then did not track the run properly. Llorente now has five goals on this ground.

The idea that Atletico Madrid are focused on spoiling and nullifying belongs in the past. They are an attractive team, well organised and you suspect they have the gears to cause Liverpool problems... and as we type, they have just opened the scoring by playing straight through Liverpool’s middle. It was a bad goal for home side to concede. Milos Kerkez was out of sync with the rest of Liverpool’s defence and Marcos Llorente has galloped straight through. As we mentioned at the start: it’s a substantial test for the hosts... it’s just got even bigger.

A little line about Llorente, who has now scored five times against Liverpool in the Champions League. He is fond of playing in this arena, he named his dog “Anfield! when he bought it in 2021.

According to recent reports, chance for Barcola. Szoboszlai clips a lovely ball in behind down the right channel to pick out the run of Barcola. The Frenchman takes it down beautifully before having his shot saved by Oblak. Barcola’s best moment thus far tonight.

Baena takes a first-time effort on from a central position around 25 yards out but he cannot keep his effort down and it sails into The Kop.

Atletico were renowned for years under Diego Simeone is being very tight at the back and in midfield, especially away from home. However, in recent years they have become more expansive and as a result are more open.

It has been revealed that liverpool win their first corner of the night at the Anfield Road End in front of the travelling Atletico fans. They take it short and Szoboslzai takes it towards the Atletico box. It appeared to be a very obvious foul on Szoboszlai right on the edge of the box but nothing is given. At the very least, it should have been given a free-kick as there was definitely at least one foul.

Barcola, who has won the Champions League with PSG in the last two seasons, is starting out on the right for Liverpool tonight with Ngumoha on the left.

It has been revealed that significant test for Liverpool and it will be fascinating to see how this formation works out. It looks very much like it is 4-4-2, with Florian Wirtz almost alongside Alexander Isak and Rio Ngumoha the left winger and Bradley Barcola on the opposite flank - a position Andoni Iraola has referenced him playing in Lyon as a teenager. It’s also a big test for Iraola against Diego Simeone, the wily and vastly experienced manager, who is immaculately dressed - as always - in his trademark black suit.

Liverpool have a chance inside the opening minute. Szoboszlai wins it inside his own half and drives forward. He then plays it out to his right to find Isak, whose shot from the right side of the box is dragged wide of the far post. Isak did score from a similar position against Ipswich last Friday, when he scored at the near post.

A minute’s silence to remember the victims of the landslides in Nepal is impeccably observed.

We are under way at Anfield. Liverpool’s Champions League campaign gets going as Andoni Iraola takes charge of his first game as a manager in this competition.

Recent findings suggest that the two sides emerge from the tunnel to a cacophony of noise and we are moments away from kick-off at Anfield. The home fans boo the Champions League anthem and belt out “Liverpool! Liverpool!” over the top of it. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:.

The original “This is Anfield” sign has sold at auction for almost £150,000, 10 times more than its guide price.

The sign that hung above the players’ tunnel at Liverpool’s home stadium during the 1970s had been expected to fetch between £10,000 and £15,000 after being put up for auction on Tuesday and Wednesday.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

Recent findings suggest that the Argentine is into the final two years of his contract, which runs out in 2028. He arrived at Liverpool in the same summer as fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, who have both signed new contracts. Mac Allister was linked with a move away from Liverpool during the summer transfer window and was candid about his contractual situation in the press conference yesterday:.

Recent findings suggest that “I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a newly introduced contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad. Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

“I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I did not get mine. Of course, there is still time. The fans do not need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”.

Industry observers note that former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez, who led the club to Champions League glory on that famous night in Istanbul in 2005, is in attendance tonight. Andoni Iraola has just shared a hug with his compatriot and perhaps Benitez will have a few words of advice for Iraola ahead of his Champions League debut as a manager.

The Dutchman has been in fine form at the start of the season for Liverpool, registering a goal and three assists in his first three games. He missed training yesterday and is not in Liverpool’s matchday squad tonight. Andoni Iraola has confirmed that Gakpo has a small adductor injury that he picked up in the Ipswich game last Friday but could be fit for the weekend against Fulham.

When Liverpool won their sixth European Cup in 2019, they lifted it in the Wanda Metropolitano against Tottenham. This season’s Champions League final is in that very stadium and Liverpool’s Champions League campaign starts tonight against the club that plays their home games in that stadium, Atletico Madrid.

“This is going to be a challenge, I hope, all the season because it would mean we continue in all the competitions. In this case, it is not the worst scenario because we played last Friday so we have had I think a good recovery. Probably it is going to be more difficult for next weekend, especially for the next game against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup because we will have just two days, game, two days, game. Recent findings suggest that liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

According to recent reports, andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

“I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola said. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a big challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

“It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a substantial responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”.

Atletico Madrid presently sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

It has been revealed that “We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone stated. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”.
